title: Spotlight Tour: Thresholds, with Jane Lilly ’27
description: On this tour, Jane Lilly ’27 will discuss boundaries and in-betweenness, exploring how we see and move through works of art. The stops on the tour include a lintel (Fez, Morocco, Marinid period, early to mid-14th century); a stained glass window, titled Scene from the Life of Thomas Becket (Canterbury, England, c. 1190–1205); and the painting Piazza San Marco, Venice (c. 1730–34) by Canaletto. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: STUDIO STAGE: Alexa Connelly, soprano | My Heart is a Garden | Graduating Student Project
description: “This recital is a reflection of growth and finding yourself again in the process of becoming. After a year of unexpected challenges with my voice and a lot of growth along the way, I’ve come to appreciate the joy of singing in a whole new way. Inspired by the patient and care of tending a garden this program explores joy, resilience, and new beginnings.” Alexa Connelly is a student of Corrine Byrne. Soprano Alexa Connelly , originally from New Hampshire, is known for her rich-toned lyricism and expressive artistry in opera, oratorio, and art song. She earned her Bachelor of Music in Vocal Performance from the University of New Hampshire, showcasing her talent as a soloist in Brahms Requiem and taking on lead roles as Suor Angelica in Suor Angelica , Belinda in Dido and Aeneas , and The Fence in Considering Matthew Shepard . In 2023, Alexa celebrated a significant milestone by winning the UNH Aria and Concerto Competition, dazzling the audience with her rendition of “Ain’t It a Pretty Night?” alongside the UNH Wind Symphony. Her dedication and passion for music have earned her several Granite State and New England NATS awards. Currently she is pursuing her Masters at The Longy School of Music at Bard College where she has had the privilege to join Vox Exchange, a chamber ensemble working closely with the Grammy-nominated Lorelei Ensemble. title: Jim Infantino, Terry Kitchen, Jack Byrne at McCarthy's Sunday Oct 11
description: Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents singer/songwriters Jim Infantino, Terry Kitchen, and Jack Byrne on Sunday afternoon October 11. The show begins at 4:00 pm and admission is $15 in advance, $20 at the door. McCarthy's is at 1920 Mass. Ave, Cambridge, across from the Porter Square Red Line T station. For advance tickets visit https://tickets.24hourmusic.com/eventperformances.asp?evt=1866. For more information call McCarthy's at 617-945-1887, visit https://www.mccarthystoad.com/, or https://www.facebook.com/SomervilleSongwriterSessions or email SomervilleSongwriterSessions@gmail.com. Somerville Songwriter Sessions at McCarthy's presents contemporary folk singer/songwriters in concert on the second Sunday afternoon of each month. Each performer will do a solo set, followed by a round-robin with all three performers. McCarthy's features live music in a comfortable, listening room setting, and features a full menu and bar. Our 10/11 performers: Jim Infantino has been performing his own brand of off-kilter folk music since the '80s when he was an underage teen sneaking into Dave Van Ronk's open mic at The Speakeasy on Macdougal Street. His songs have been described as satirical, witty, sardonic, urbane, funny, heartbreaking, catchy, philosophical and razor sharp. Sometimes political, sometimes personal, sometimes abstract, his songs weave in the hint of humor when you expect sadness and tragedy when you expect levity. Since 1996 he has been performing both solo and with his band Jim's Big Ego, who describe themselves as "the greatest band in the history of recorded music." With the band he has released 7 full-length CDs adding to his 4 solo releases including his latest, 2025's Assemble Yourself. He is also a novelist, with his debut book The Wakeful Wanderer's Guide to New New England and Beyond winning the 2017 Wattys Newcomer's Award, and its sequel, The Wakeful Wanderer's Guide to Disillusionment, appearing in 2021. More on Jim at jiminfantino.co

African and Caribbean dance traditions are rooted in the diverse cultures of countries such as Madagascar, Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad & Tobago, and Cuba, among many others. Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. title: Physical Math Seminar
description: Speaker: Nicolas Romeo (University of Chicago) Title: Mechanical canalization of chiral morphogenesis Abstract: A developing embryo reliably builds the same intricate body plan, time after time, from thousands of noisy, heterogeneous cells driven by stochastic molecular signals and mechanical forces. How internal organs such as the gut break left-right symmetry with a reproducible handedness remains unclear. I will present results of a theory-experiment collaboration to understand the mechanisms of the reproducible coiling of the fruit fly midgut, in which mechanics and geometry play a starring role. We find that an initial constriction phase bias the initial symmetry breaking, with handedness determined by an inter-organ relay of molecular cues. Organ elongation under anatomical confinement then drives a controlled buckling instability, both amplifying and stabilizing coiling geometry. These results point to a ‘mechanical Waddington landscape’, in which molecular inputs bias the organ towards one of two chiral outcomes that are then canalized by mechanical constraints. More broadly, these findings suggest that tissue-scale mechanics can serve as a source of developmental robustness and thus help make anatomy reproducible.

title: Yang Tan Collective, Brain-Body Center Seminar: Sung-Yon Kim, Seoul National University
description: Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 Time: 3:00 – 4:00 pm Location: Building 46, Singleton Auditorium Talk Title: How does drinking rapidly quench thirst? Abstract: Drinking quenches thirst within seconds, long before ingested water can restore systemic fluid balance, but the sensory origin and neural mechanisms underlying this rapid feedback have remained unclear. We identify pharyngeal mechanosensation generated during swallowing as a key sensory signal for rapid thirst satiation. This signal depends primarily on PIEZO2 in pharynx-projecting sensory neurons and ascends through the NTS and Pdyn+ parabrachial neurons to Glp1r+ MnPO neurons, ultimately suppressing SFO thirst neurons and terminating ongoing drinking. Notably, this pathway does not simply relay every swallow. Instead, it implements rate-dependent filtering that preferentially transmits rapidly repeated, drinking-paced swallows while excluding slower patterns associated with eating. Together, these findings define a pharynx-to-forebrain circuit that transforms swallowing-related mechanical signals into rapid, drinking-specific homeostatic feedback.

title: The Tobacco Takers: Puritans, Pipes, and Bodily Care
description: Free Hybrid Lecture Speakers: Diana DiPaolo Loren , Deputy Director for Curatorial Affairs and Senior Curator, Peabody Museum, Harvard University Stephen W. Silliman , Professor, Department of Anthropology, University of Massachusetts Boston Indigenous to the Americas and cultivated by Native peoples for thousands of years, tobacco was introduced to Europeans in the 16th century, and by the early 17th century, it had spread across the globe. In Puritan New England, religious leaders condemned tobacco as sinful while early practitioners used it as medicine. Clay tobacco pipes commonly found at 17th-century archaeological sites in Massachusetts reveal widespread use despite strict social and religious restrictions. Drawing from her new book, The Tobacco Takers: Puritanism, Smoking, Health, and the Archaeology of Bodily Care (Bloomsbury Publishing, 2026), Diana DiPaolo Loren will share archaeological, archival, and visual evidence that recasts tobacco and tobacco pipes as tools of bodily care for both physical and metaphysical ailments. The program will include a conversation with archaeologist Stephen W. Silliman. Copies of The Tobacco Takers will be available for purchase after the program. Advance registration is recommended for online and in-person attendance. Free event parking is available with registration at the 52 Oxford Street Garage , starting at 5:00 pm. Register by October 12th, 2026 to receive parking registration instructions. Presented by the Peabody Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology and the Harvard Museums of Science & Culture. About the Speakers Diana DiPaolo Loren (PhD, State University of New York at Binghamton) is Deputy Director for Curatorial Affairs and Senior Curator at the Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology, Harvard University. Loren specializes in the colonial northeastern United States, with a focus on the body, health, dress, and adornment. title: An Ocean (Re)Introduction
description: Emmy Award-winning storyteller and explorer Richard Vevers invites you to see the ocean in a completely new way. Best known for his work on the Netflix documentary Chasing Coral and for pioneering Google Street View underwater, Vevers now leads Room 71 at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, an initiative transforming how we understand and communicate ocean science. In this talk, Vevers challenges what we think we know about the ocean. Drawing on insights from leading oceanographers and explorers, he reveals how human perception often distorts our understanding of the vast and dynamic world beneath the surface. Through compelling stories and imagery, he reintroduces the ocean as it truly is—complex, surprising, and deeply connected to our lives. title: Pınar Öğrenci: Good Luck in Germany
description: The 2026 Busch-Reisinger Museum Lecture Berlin-based artist and filmmaker Pınar Öğrenci will discuss her 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany), which is featured in her first major exhibition in the United States, here at the Harvard Art Museums. The film examines the construction of postwar German identity in the Ruhrgebiet, a heavily industrialized region known for coal mining and steel production, as shaped by layered experiences of survival, resistance, and resilience. In it, Öğrenci applies a feminist lens, broadening the history of industrial labor beyond the male worker and the factory. The lecture brings Glück auf in Deutschland into conversation with Öğrenci’s other films, exploring filmmaking as a political practice through which the history of “guest workers” can be connected to ongoing struggles around labor, migration, and belonging. The exhibition Pınar Öğrenci: Glück auf in Deutschland (April 16, 2026–October 18, 2026) includes the 2024 film Glück auf in Deutschland (Good Luck in Germany) as well as five related collages that reimagine the bodies of workers and their families within the Ruhr landscape and its architecture. Öğrenci’s use of the phrase Glück auf—a common way that miners wish one another a safe return after their physically grueling and dangerous work underground—resonates with the experiences of immigrant communities in present-day Germany facing right-wing extremism. Following the program, guests are invited to visit the exhibition on Level 1. This lecture will be recorded and made available for online viewing; check back shortly after the event for the link to view. This event is part of In Conversation, a series of evening programs that feature local and international curators, artists, scholars, and more. Running from September through April, these events highlight our temporary exhibitions, permanent collections, and a range of creative voices. title: SOLD OUT! Lectures On Tap: “Neuroscientist Explains: The Modules of the Mind”
description: Lectures On Tap: “Neuroscientist Explains: The Modules of the Mind” Event Description: 🎤 Speaker: Michael Cohen We tend to think of the brain as a general-purpose, endlessly adaptable supercomputer. In reality, it’s far stranger and more fascinating. The brain isn’t one big machine at all, but a collection of quirky specialists—distinct modules, each with its own narrow job and responsibilities. When one of these specialists goes offline due to stroke, accident, or disease, the results can be startling. Some people can no longer recognize faces, even their own. Others lose the ability to feel fear while every other emotion remains intact. Some can’t understand other people’s intentions, while others see their moral compass and personal values radically change. In this engaging talk, neuroscientist Michael Cohen will guide you on a tour of these hidden specialists in your head: the modules that let you recognize a smile, feel empathy, and navigate the social world. By the end, you’ll gain a clearer picture not only of how your brain is organized, but of the fundamental structures that shape your own mind. Michael Cohen is a Professor of Neuroscience and Psychology at Amherst College and a Research Scientist at MIT. title: Bandits on the Run
description: Bandits on the Run are a musical trio from the Brooklyn-Queens border. Born from a chance encounter busking on the subway, Adrian Blake Enscoe, Sydney Shepherd, and Regina Strayhorn defy convention with an impressive trade-off of lead vocals and instruments. The Bandits marry acoustic, electric, and bass guitar sounds with cello, accordion, suitcases-turned-kickdrums, and (if you’re lucky) sometimes even a megaphone. The Bandit’s three-part harmonies have been heard filling iconic venues while opening for The Wood Brothers’ 2025 East Coast tour, on the main stages at Colorado’s Rocky Mount Folks Fest and Michigan’s Blissfest, and in a sold out residency at Manhattan’s Bowery Electric. Their songs have been featured by NPR’s Tiny Desk and The Moth Story Slam, as well as in Netflix’s Ask the StoryBots and the feature film The Same Storm. The Bandits tour nationally and internationally, with appearances at Cambridge Folk Festival, Floydfest, Summerfest Milwaukee, Americanafest, F1 Singapore Grand Prix, Mile of Music, and more. Their theatrical indie-folk lends itself quite well to storytelling and their work adapting text for a musical production of As You Like It later became their EP The Shakespeare Tapes. In addition to all their touring and recording work, Bandits on the Run are also in the business of writing musicals, sometimes as a trio and sometimes with collaborators. They are currently creating the stage musical adaptation of the novel What’s Eating Gilbert Grape with actor-musician-longtime friend Christopher Sears and newfound friend Academy Award Nominee Peter Hedges, supported by MCC Theater. Bandits on the Run are also developing an original musical, Yukon Ho, about a group of Black prospectors in the Alaskan gold rush, Yukon Ho was researched on the ground in Skagway, Alaska with support from the NEA, and has been workshopped with support from Prospect Musicals. They are alumni of several musical theater writing development programs, including Berkeley

Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. title: Lie Groups Seminar
description: Speaker: Daniel Litt (University of Toronto) Title: Exceptional motives and exceptional local systems Abstract: In 1996, Serre asked about the existence of motives with exceptional motivic Galois group. Such motives are now known to exist for all exceptional groups, due to work of Gross–Savin, Katz, Dettweiler–Reiter, Yun, Patrikis, Boxer–Calegari–Emerton–Levin– Patrikis–Madapusi Pera, Guralnick–Lubeck–Yu, and Faegerman (and possibly others). For all exceptional groups except E6, families of such motives were known, but until recently this was open for E6. I’ll survey this story, explain joint work with Krämer–Maculan constructing families of exceptional E6-motives—arising from the classical geometry of cubic 3-folds—and speculate about similar constructions for other exceptional groups.

description: Classes will be broken into 5 sections at Level 1. New sessions start the first Monday of every odd month. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Bad Words Book Bash with Ríoghnach Robinson
description: Bad Words follows critic Selina Chan, whose blistering review turned Parker Navarro’s debut novel into the flop of the decade. Four years later, his new book offers a chance at redemption, but her second takedown sparks a viral literary feud. As the publishing world feasts on their public rivalry, a quieter dialogue begins—one that challenges their ideas about success, sincerity, and each other. Incisive and tender, Bad Words lays bare the costs of creation, the tension between ambition and integrity, the vulnerability of being seen, and the unexpected closeness between critique and care. In conversation with local Bookstagrammer Jess Lee, Ríoghnach will discuss writing romance born from rivalry, the culture of publishing and literary criticism, and the ways public narratives can shape private relationships. Following the author talk, stick around for a meet and greet with the author. Ríoghnach will sign and personalize Bad Words as well as up to two titles brought from home. 6:30 PM: Doors Open – Settle in to your seat and work on a Bad Words themed activity sheet while you wait for the discussion to begin! 7:00 PM: Discussion Begins – Ríoghnach and Jess will dive into Bad Words. 7:45 PM: Q&A Session – Your chance to ask the author anything! 8:00 PM: Signatures, Snapping Pics, and Salutations – Meet the author , get your book signed, snap a photo, and feel free to shop the store for your next favorite read! 8:30 PM : Head to the register to make any final purchases. 9:00 PM: Event Wraps Up – Thanks for joining us!

description: The goal of this class is to build technical competence through drills and choreographies as well as self-expression, musicality, fluidity, and stamina. REGISTER HERE We accept payments online in addition to those made in-person Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo (@SambaViva), PayPal (sambaviva@gmail.com), Credit Card What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Samba is a rhythm and a dance that exudes equal parts beauty, spirituality, and resistance. Borne in Brazil from enslaved Africans, samba has spread to the mainstream and is now one of the country’s most famous exports. Samba is constantly evolving in all of its forms; currently there are many popular samba sub-genres, including pagode, samba rock, bossa nova, etc. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? SambaViva teachers have a minimum of 5 (and as many as 20!) years dancing and training samba and other Brazilian styles. title: Solo Aging Series (Virtual)
description: Join Marni Blank, founder of Begin with the End, for a three-part series designed to give solo agers and those preparing for that possibility the practical tools, emotional support, and community connection they need to plan with confidence. title: Symplectic Geometry Seminar
description: Samuel Sottille (Stanford University) Title: Almost Toric Fibrations in Higher Dimensions Abstract: The SYZ conjecture posits that special Lagrangian fibrations provide a geometric explanation for mirror symmetry. On the purely symplectic side, non-special Lagrangian torus fibrations provide a useful framework for understanding the geometry of symplectic manifolds. However, there is no general theory of these fibrations in dimensions higher than four. In this talk, I will present my results on constructing Lagrangian torus fibrations in higher dimensions. I will show that a wide class of manifolds with toric degenerations admit almost toric fibrations. I will show that Gross and Siebert's combinatorial duality for toric degenerations can be realized as a duality of these almost toric fibrations. I will construct almost toric fibrations on all three-dimensional Fano varieties. Time permitting, I will present applications to computing disk potentials of monotone torus fibers.

title: Celebrating Neil Pappalardo
description: Honoring the late A. Neil Pappalardo’s impact on MIT Celebrating Neil Pappalardo Thursday, October 15, 5:30pm Thomas Tull Concert Hall, Linde Music Building by MIT Video Productions of MIT Open Learning and MIT Music & Theater Arts Honoring the late A. Neil Pappalardo’s impact on MIT, this event features a tribute film produced by MIT Video Productions and special music performances by MIT faculty and students. Free and open to the public. Please reserve seats. A native of New York state, with interests in astrophysics, cosmology, and electrical engineering, Neil Pappalardo (1942-2026) was the founder and CEO of MEDITECH, a leading supplier of information systems for 2,200 hospitals in the U.S., Europe, Australia, and Africa. His career was spent in product development, creating software that allows health care providers to track each patient’s history and monitor ongoing treatment for chronic health problems, regardless of the patient’s location. MIT class of 1964, Neil was an MIT Corporation life member and Executive Committee member whose passion for the Institute was reflected by his extensive volunteer engagement, his joyful, hands-on approach, his often-uncanny ability to know what the Institute needed, and his willingness to identify and enable talent at MIT. Please join us for a post-event reception in the lobby.

title: Studio Ossidiana—Giovanni Bellotti and Alessandra Covini
description: Studio Ossidiana—Giovanni Bellotti and Alessandra Covini Part of the MIT Fall 2026 Architecture Lecture Series. Presented with the Architecture and Urbanism Group Studio Ossidiana is a design practice based in the Netherlands, working across scales to create spaces, objects, exhibitions, and installations at the intersection of architecture, design, art, and landscape. The studio’s projects include experimental playgrounds for children and adults, floating gardens inhabited by birds, outdoor kitchens, land art pavilions on water, to be explored and cultivated by humans and other species. Led by Alessandra Covini and Giovanni Bellotti, with Klaas van der Molen joining the studio in 2025, Studio Ossidiana collaborates with international institutions including the Centre Pompidou and the National Museum in Oslo. The studio’s work has been presented at the Venice Architecture Biennale (2021–2023), Milan Triennale (2022), Shenzhen Architecture Biennale (2022), Istanbul Design Biennial (2021), Chicago Architecture Biennial (2021), and Bruges Triennial (2024). Alongside their design practice, Giovanni and Alessandra teach at international universities, including HEAD Genève (Haute école d’art et de design), where they lead a course exploring the relationship between plants and interiors. Studio Ossidiana’s work has received numerous awards and distinctions, including the Prix de Rome (2018), the Netherlands’ oldest award for designers under 35; the Italian Architecture Under 35 Award (2023); and nominations for the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture / Mies van der Rohe Award (2024, 2026). This lecture will be held in person in the Sidara Auditorium (W41- 1216) and streamed online on YouTube. Lectures are free and open to the public. Registration is required.

title: Fireside Chat with Libbie Grant
description: Join author Libbie Grant as she chats with Internet and Identity Scholar Judith Donath about her new novel THE ENDED WORLD! Libbie Grant's THE ENDED WORLD: A young woman’s vision over a Quebec lake sends her on a search to understand her relationship to the divine. While she spends years as a cloistered nun, a young boy struggles with his Mormon upbringing and, discovering the internet, grows up to design an AI entity that stuns him by appearing sentient. Embarking on their own separate road trips, these characters unite to face the scope of their responsibilities, their understanding of what’s holy, and the very question of what it is to be a human being. Steeped in philosophy, theology, and computer science, THE ENDED WORLD is a novel for our times. Judith Donath is a writer, designer and artist whose work focuses on the co-evolution of technology and society. She has published numerous articles about social media, AI, ethics and anonymity, and is the author of The Social Machine: Designs for Living Online (MIT Press). As the former director of the MIT Media Lab's Sociable Media Group, she and her students designed innovative interfaces for on-line communities; their art projects examining the future of identity, privacy and mediated life have been exhibited in museums and galleries worldwide. Currently, she is a faculty fellow at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center and is writing a book about technology, trust and deception.

description: Beginner House introduces students to house music, and house dance fundamentals. No experience is required! One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. title: In-Person Bellydance
description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. Experience the power of fiery hip-locks and shimmies, and the fluid beauty of serpentine undulations. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. Instructions: Wear comfortable dance or workout clothing that allows you to move freely. Classes are danced barefoot or in dance shoes. Students will be encouraged to acquire a veil and finger cymbals (zsagaat/ills). Cash preferred, or Venmo Drop-ins always welcome! What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. Tap is an American dance form in which rhythms are audibly tapped out on the floor. It has origins in slavery and the percussive dances of West African Juba dance and Irish step dancing. It developed through minstrel shows and vaudeville in the late 19th century and emerged along with jazz in the 20th century into the art form we know today. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Sela has been a tap teacher since 2000, taking over Maureen Cosgrove’s Boston Tap classes at the Dance Complex in 2014. While at Smith College she studied in the Five College Dance Department, performing with the Celebrations Dance Company and the UMass University Dancers. She was a founding member of the Terpsichore Ensemble in Amherst, MA and taught tap classes in Amherst and Northampton, MA before moving to Boston. Sela teaches adult beginner and intermediate tap classes at the Dance Complex, and made her Dance Complex choreographic debut at the 2018 Spring Teaching Artists and Student Concert with students from the intermediate tap class. title: MAIN STAGE: Wayman Chin | Sweet Land | Faculty Artist Recital
description: “Sweet land, we sing to thee….” Mirrored reflections on the mystic chords of memory As we look back on the 250 years since the founding of our nation, we hold a mirror of hopes cast and yet to be realized, all generated by a spirit of intensity, invention, and re-invention. To mark our nation’s semiquincentennial, faculty pianist and Dean Emeritus Wayman Chin presents a program of pieces that reflect the American psyche, including works by Aaron Copland, Samuel Barber and Leonard Bernstein; Beethoven’s Seven Variations on “God Save the King,” (to whose melody Samuel Francis Smith penned new lyrics we know as “My Country, ’tis of thee”) and contemporary composers Jeremy Van Buskirk and Nico Muhly, whose “Refine” for solo piano is a short variation on “America the Beautiful.” Main Stage Series Main Stage events are where the magic happens. Experience performances that inspire, challenge, and resonate long after the final note. You’ll hear bold artistic ideas and exceptional musicianship, often featuring Longy’s distinguished faculty-artists and innovative artistic partners. Each event offers a rare opportunity to be part of artistry that is both inspirational in the moment and lasting in its impact. Longy’s performance are free and open to the public, but please register in advance.

title: Oktoberfest: Choucroute & American Wines – Wine Tasting Class
description: What should you drink with choucroute when the wines are American? Join internationally renowned sommelier Bertil Jean-Chronberg for a lively 90-minute wine-and-food experience inspired by the convivial spirit of a German wine hall. Explore how different styles of American wine interact with the richness of sausages and pork, the acidity of sauerkraut, mustard, spices and all the savory complexity of this classic dish. Taste several contrasting American wines alongside choucroute and discover why acidity, sweetness, aromatic intensity and texture can completely change a pairing. More importantly, learn how to recognize what works, and why. So, you can apply the same principles to your own table. As always at Bonde, expect serious wine without the seriousness: only 16 participants, generous conversation, plenty of tasting, food and wine, and a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere where there are no wrong questions. Prost! Please inform us in advance of any food allergies or dietary restrictions. We will do our best but cannot guarantee accommodation for all restrictions. Salsa is a musical and dance style that originated in Cuba with African roots and European influences. It later developed in New York and it’s popular throughout Latin America in places like Puerto Rico, Colombia, Peru and Cuba just to name a few. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I grew up listening to Salsa music and later got interested in the dance. As a teenager, I was part of a Colombian folk dance group before starting to perform Salsa duets with my brother Andres. I’ve been teaching Salsa for about 27 years now and this year we are celebrating 23 years of our dance company, Salsa y Control. Finish this statement: I am passionate about teaching this style because… It allows people to connect in a unique way. Salsa dancing is a social dance that help break barriers and brings people together from all walks of life. It also gives you the opportunity to express yourself freely on the dance floor or stage. description: The Intermediate House class is for students who have learned basic house concepts/vocabulary and/or are comfortable learning independently in dance class. One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. title: SCSB Lunch Series with Dr. Tatsuya Osaki: Modeling Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity and Hemodynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder with an iPSC-Derived Microphysiological System
description: Date: Friday, October 16, 2026 Time: 12:00pm – 1:00pm Location: Simons Center Conference room 46-6011. Zoom: https://mit.zoom.us/j/99705232954 Speaker: Tatsuya Osaki, Ph.D. Affiliation: Research Scientist, Mriganka Sur Laboratory, Picower Institute for Learning and Memory, MIT Talk title: Modeling Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity and Hemodynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder with an iPSC-Derived Microphysiological System Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) encompasses a diverse group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by challenges in social interaction, cognition, and communication. While neuronal dysfunction has been extensively studied, the role of vascular dysregulation, particularly blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity and cerebrovascular hemodynamics during early development, remains largely unexplored. Using Rett syndrome (RTT) as a disease entry point, we demonstrate that mutations in methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MeCP2) impair endothelial cell function, suggesting a vascular-intrinsic contribution to pathogenesis. To investigate this, we developed a human iPSC-derived microphysiological system recapitulating BBB structure and function in a physiologically relevant 3D environment. Patient-derived endothelial cells carrying MeCP2 mutations self-assembled into perfusable microvascular networks, revealing significant impairment in vascular barrier function, independently validated in MeCP2 knockout mouse models. Transcriptomic analysis identified aberrant upregulation of miR-126 and loss of tight junction integrity as key mediators of BBB dysfunction. Targeted inhibition of miR-126-3p restored barrier function, establishing it as a novel therapeutic candidate. Building on these findings, we are expanding this platform to model hemodynamic alterations across broader ASD subtypes, with in vivo cross-validation via two-photon microscopy, aiming to uncover shared neurovascular mechanisms and identify therapeutic targets for ASD and related neurodevelopm

title: Our Own Language / Lang a nou — Book Launch & Public Conversation
description: Celebrate MIT Prof. Michel DeGraff’s new book _Our Own Language / Lang a nou_. Introductory remarks, conversation & book signing. OUR OWN LANGUAGE / LANG A NOU A Book Launch & Public Conversation with Michel DeGraff and Haynes Miller. Introduced and Moderated by M. S. Vijay Kumar. What happens when children are denied the right to learn in the language they know best? What becomes possible when communities reclaim their own languages as tools for knowledge, education, human rights, dignity, democracy, liberation and nation-building? Join us at the MIT Museum for a special evening celebrating the publication of Michel DeGraff’s new MIT Press book, written in English and Kreyòl: Our Own Language: Harnessing the Power of Kreyòl and Other Mother Tongues for Education and Liberation Lang a nou: Kreyòl ak lòt lang manman se zouti pou edikasyon ak liberasyon Drawing on Haiti’s revolutionary history, the struggle for Kreyòl in education, and the predicament of post-colonies around the world, Our Own Language / Lang a nou challenges a belief with deep roots in colonial history, namely the belief that some languages — and, by implication, some people — are more worthy of access to knowledge and power than others. For this special evening, linguist, activist and author Michel DeGraff will introduce some of the stories and ideas that led him to write the book, then he and Haynes Miller will engage each other and the audience in a conversation about language, education, inequality and the possibilities afforded by Liberatory Linguistics. The conversation will be introduced and moderated by M. S. Vijay Kumar. Audience discussion will follow. Books will be available for purchase and signing. Come celebrate our languages and imagine an education where every child counts. The event is free and open to the public.

title: Listen To This: Celebrating 100 Years of Miles Davis
description: One of the pivotal moments in our music lifetimes came when Miles Davis traded in his tailored Italian suits for mod psychedelic threads, and re-engineered his music with grooves from Sly Stone and James Brown and guitars from Jimi Hendrix. Created with a parade of genius collaborators, In a Silent Way, Bitches Brew, Jack Johnson, Live/Evil, On the Corner and other albums wrote new playbooks for jazz improvisers. Out of that matrix emerged multiple lineages, but nobody ever did it quite like Miles and company. The eight members of Listen to This revive, refresh and inhabit this music fearlessly. Led by Morphine’s founding drummer Jerome Deupree, LTT features Ornette Coleman keyboardist Dave Bryant, Either/Orchestra leader Russ Gershon on woodwinds and organ, Bim Skala Bim percussionist Rick Barry, trumpeter Bryan Murphy, bassist Rick McLaughlin, guitarist J. Johnson, and Todd Brunel in the essential and mysterious bass clarinet role.

description: $15 admission / 10:15 doors / 10:30 show / seated & standing / all ages Phoenix's Debut Album "Glass Rose" is a 10 song story concept album that walks through the lifetime of an abusive relationship from meeting to murder. Phoenix Davis (they/them) is a queer disabled singer songwriter who creates and performs music to make people feel less alone. They have been performing and writing since they were 7 years old and they are currently working on getting degrees in Performance and Professional Music with concentrations in Music Business, Music Production, and Songwriting from Berklee College of Music. As a queer disabled person, they strive to create inclusive music experiences that anyone can feel heard and seen in whether that be a gender neutral love song, or a song showcasing the trials of life as a disabled person. This show will center around their Debut album "Glass Rose", a story album telling the story of a toxic relationship and the main character regaining their inner strength. title: Nature and Mount Auburn
description: Join us for a mindful walk through the landscape, exploring the history and founding of Mount Auburn Cemetery. From its beginning, Mount Auburn Cemetery has drawn on nature as a resource for comfort, a focus of study, and a guide for developing its sacred landscape. Its founding, in 1831, influenced the expansion of garden cemeteries, the future development of landscape architecture, and the national park movement. This tour will include visits to the Asa Gray Garden, Consecration Dell, and the monuments of Jacob Bigelow, Margaret Fuller, and Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. Expect to enhance your understanding of the cemetery’s rich history, and learn how the study of botany, transcendentalism, and environmental neuroscience has helped us to understand the ways that nature sustains and inspires us. Tour Guide: Barry J. Kahn Barry J. Kahn is one of twenty volunteer docents who staff the Welcome Center at Mount Auburn Cemetery. When he retired as a social worker in July 2025, Barry began to create a tour centered on illuminating how places, like Mount Auburn Cemetery, promote peace of mind. Comfortable walking shoes recommended. title: MIT / French Library Author Series: Before I Forget with Anne Pauly
description: Anne Pauly is a Paris-based French writer and winner of the Prix du Livre Inter and Prix Robert Walser. Her debut novel, Before I Forget, was also shortlisted for the Prix Goncourt, Prix Femina, and Prix Wepler. Before turning to fiction, she worked as a journalist and wrote on music, feminism, queer culture, and literature. In Before I Forget, Pauly recounts the aftermath of her father’s death and the complicated task of mourning a man who was at once a self-taught philosopher and romantic, and an alcoholic whose violence marked his family. As Anne sorts through his belongings and prepares his funeral, she tries to reconcile these contradictory versions of the man she has lost. Told with wit and tenderness, the novel is a tragicomic exploration of grief, family, class, and the complicated bonds between parents and children. The conversation will be moderated by Bruno Perreau, Cynthia L. Reed Professor of French Studies at MIT and a specialist in contemporary French literature and culture, critical theory, and politics. He is the author of thirteen books, including Queer Theory: The French Response and, most recently, Spheres of Injustice: The Ethical Promise of Minority Presence (MIT Press, 2025).

title: Conversations: Above and Beneath, An Ode to Women Artists
description: Detritus dance performs a site-responsive dance installation in dialogue with women artists in Mount Auburn’s landscape, past and present. Detritus dance activates the landscape of Mount Auburn Cemetery through a site-responsive, roaming contemporary dance installation entitled “Conversations: Above and Beneath.” Inspired by Margaret Fuller Ossoli’s “Conversations”, a series of assemblies between 1839-1844 of Bostonian women who sought alternate means of education when it was formally denied to them, our “movement salon” pays homage to the radical 19th-century Bostonian women artists of significance in Mount Auburn’s burial grounds. Our performance interweaves the connected narratives of writer Margaret Fuller Ossoli; poet Maria White Lowell; actor Charlotte Cushman; sculptor Edmonia Lewis; and historian Hannah Adams. We seek to bring these women’s stories into dialogue with our own across place and time, and in doing so help to reshape the ways we publicly memorialize women’s stories. This performance will make stops at: Maria White Lowell’s gravesite, the Hygeia Statue, Hannah Adam’s gravesite; Margaret Fuller Ossoli’s cenotaph, and Hazel Dell. Attendees are encouraged to wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. Accessible accommodations will be provided. About the Artists-in-Residence: Detritus dance is a company focused on embodied storytelling through dance and multidisciplinary performance. Founded in 2021 by Caroline Bradbury and Claire Lane, we are a queer and women-led organization who strive to amplify intersectional feminist and queer narratives through our work. Detritus is defined as “a product of disintegration, destruction, or wearing away.” Our name alludes to how we activate our performance by incorporating elements of visual collage and writing in our research process. description: This event is at capacity. Join us for a special gallery talk that includes a walking tour! Graduate student teacher Ryan Schmidt-Knapik will first discuss the exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors in the galleries before leading a walking tour on campus, where you will learn how to interpret and appreciate nature in our urban landscape. We will focus on exploring how plant form, function, and the history of non-native species introduction have shaped the biology of human-dominated landscapes. Led by: Ryan Schmidt-Knapik, Graduate student teacher and Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, Harvard University On Location: Drawing the Outdoors features drawings by J. M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. The catalogue was made possible by the Andrew W. Mellon Publication Funds. Additional project support was provided by the Almathea Charitable Foundation.

description: $20 advance / $25 door / 7:30 doors / 8pm show / seated & standing Celebrate the release of the Talking Hearts' new album, Memory Lane , with a live performance in an intimate setting! The Talking Hearts are a cutting-edge honky tonk band from Boston. Channeling the spirit of country music icons Loretta Lynn, Buck Owens, and George Jones, the Talking Hearts play witty and relatable original songs written by fiddler Rachel Rosenberg about folks who’ve done her wrong. Their new album, Memory Lane , showcases the thick three-part harmony singing of Rachel, Zach Meyer (mandolin, piano), and Sophie Wellington (guitar), while bassist Dan Bui and drummer Mike Harmon lay down an infectious rhythmic groove and Alex Formento adds that sweet lonesome texture on pedal steel and telecaster. At this rare chance to hear the Talking Hearts perform new music in an intimate listening room, prepare to be transported to an early 1960s honky tonk, going back and forth between falling in love with your dance partner and contemplating your fate over yet another round at the bar. www.thetalkingheartsband.com

title: Radius Ensemble: Textures
description: MARY KOUYOUMDJIAN – Studies on Rage for Each Day of the Week for flute, bassoon and piano (2025) JONATHAN RUSSELL – Quintet for Clarinet and Strings (2026) WORLD PREMIERE RADIUS CO-COMMISSION CAROLINE SHAW – Limestone and Felt for viola and cello (2012) FRANCIS POULENC – Sextet for piano and winds (1932) “The world has gone bananas,” says Armenian-American composer Mary Kouyoumdjian. Her response? Studies on Rage for Each Day of the Week for flute, bassoon and piano, a looping, cacophonous work that opens Textures, the first concert of Radius Ensemble’s 28th Season. Next is the world premiere of a Radius co-commission by Jonathan Russell, his Quintet for clarinet and strings. Limestone and Felt, a duo for viola and cello by Pulitzer Prize-winner Caroline Shaw, presents a clash of textures exploring, as Shaw says, the “opposing ways we experience history and design our own present.” Francis Poulenc’s raucous Sextet for piano and winds brings the concert to a joyful close. description: Join Stefanie Haug , LICSW, ecotherapist and nature and meditation teacher as we step into the restorative beauty of Mount Auburn Cemetery for a gentle, guided mindful nature walk. title: “Worthy to be Any Man’s Friend”: Lecture on Henry David Thoreau
description: Join historian Richard Smith for a lecture in Story Chapel on Henry David Thoreau and notable figures in Mount Auburn. Henry David Thoreau was one of the most important and influential writers of the 19th Century. And while he isn’t buried in Mount Auburn Cemetery, he was well acquainted with many of the literary and political figures who are. Join Concord historian Richard Smith for a presentation about Henry Thoreau and some of his famous friends. The “Hermit of Walden Pond” wasn’t such a hermit after all. Longfellow, Charles Sumner and Margaret Fuller are just some of the notable figures who are buried here that Thoreau knew and associated with. And he even liked some of them! title: Conversations: Above and Beneath, An Ode to Women Artists
description: Detritus dance performs a site-responsive dance installation in dialogue with women artists in Mount Auburn’s landscape, past and present. Detritus dance activates the landscape of Mount Auburn Cemetery through a site-responsive, roaming contemporary dance installation entitled “Conversations: Above and Beneath.” Inspired by Margaret Fuller Ossoli’s “Conversations”, a series of assemblies between 1839-1844 of Bostonian women who sought alternate means of education when it was formally denied to them, our “movement salon” pays homage to the radical 19th-century Bostonian women artists of significance in Mount Auburn’s burial grounds. Our performance interweaves the connected narratives of writer Margaret Fuller Ossoli; poet Maria White Lowell; actor Charlotte Cushman; sculptor Edmonia Lewis; and historian Hannah Adams. We seek to bring these women’s stories into dialogue with our own across place and time, and in doing so help to reshape the ways we publicly memorialize women’s stories. This performance will make stops at: Maria White Lowell’s gravesite, the Hygeia Statue, Hannah Adam’s gravesite; Margaret Fuller Ossoli’s cenotaph, and Hazel Dell. Attendees are encouraged to wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. Accessible accommodations will be provided. About the Artists-in-Residence: Detritus dance is a company focused on embodied storytelling through dance and multidisciplinary performance. Founded in 2021 by Caroline Bradbury and Claire Lane, we are a queer and women-led organization who strive to amplify intersectional feminist and queer narratives through our work. Detritus is defined as “a product of disintegration, destruction, or wearing away.” Our name alludes to how we activate our performance by incorporating elements of visual collage and writing in our research process. title: Fireside Chat with Daisy Rockwell
description: Join author Daisy Rockwell in conversation with professor and scholar Jared Green as they discuss her new novel ALICE SEES GHOSTS! Description of ALICE SEES GHOSTS: Alice Bloodshaw’s grandmother lies dying in their crumbling ancestral home. Family relationships are fraught, and worsened by the mercurial behavior of Alice’s mother. Then Alice, eccentric and attuned to the supernatural, is haunted by the specter of her grandfather. His cryptic message sends Alice and her Bengali psychiatrist fiancé, practical-minded Ronit, on a journey from New England to India and back again to unearth the long-buried truths that have choked and tormented the family. Bit by bit, Alice untangles the past to confront the legacy of aristocracy, secrecy, and colonialism in a quest to mend family ties and stop living as a ghost herself. Biography of Jared Green: Jared Green received both his A.M. and Ph.D. from Brown University. His scholarly essays and reviews on Modernist literature, visual culture, and early cinema have been published internationally. He is also a fiction writer and experimental literary performer and has published poetry, prose poetry, children's fiction, and screenplays. He is currently a professor of English at Stonehill College, as well as the Director of their Digital Humanities Program.

title: MAIN STAGE: Dana Maiben and Vivian Montgomery | An Outburst of Improvisors | Faculty Artist Recital
description: An Outburst of Improvisors: 17th Century Music for Violin and Harpsichord In 1600s Italy, the performer and the composer were the same person, and nobody was playing it safe. Opera was being invented. The madrigal was being torn apart and rebuilt. Women were writing and publishing everywhere: on the opera stage, in their own salons, inside cloistered convents. Musicians improvised their way into an entirely new style of virtuoso songwriting, and four hundred years later it still sounds reckless. This intimate program for violin and harpsichord covers the whole range: instrumental covers of the pop songs of the day, some of the earliest violin sonatas ever written, ground-bass mash-ups, and plenty of improvising in the moment. Music by Barbara Strozzi, Biagio Marini, Chiara Margarita Cozzolani, Claudio Monteverdi, Dario Castello, Girolamo Frescobaldi, Isabella Leonarda, Marco Uccellini, Michelangelo Rossi, and Salamone Rossi, plus the premiere of a new improvisation-based work by John Morrison. Main Stage Series Main Stage events are where the magic happens. Experience performances that inspire, challenge, and resonate long after the final note. You’ll hear bold artistic ideas and exceptional musicianship, often featuring Longy’s distinguished faculty-artists and innovative artistic partners. Each event offers a rare opportunity to be part of artistry that is both inspirational in the moment and lasting in its impact. Longy’s performance are free and open to the public, but please register in advance.

title: Joe Hunt Group
description: $15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. Joe Hunt is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

title: Richard P. Stanley Seminar in Combinatorics
description: Speaker: Zilin Jiang (Arizona State University) Title: Unbalancing unit vectors Abstract: The Komlós conjecture is a prominent vector balancing problem: how can we choose signs to keep a sum of vectors small? Here we ask how large a signed sum can be guaranteed. Given n unit vectors in d-dimensional Euclidean space, with n at least d, we show that some choice of signs produces a sum of length at least √(2n − d). This resolves a conjecture of Ambrus and Nietert when n = d + 1. Our proof draws on a combinatorial form of Vaaler’s cube slicing theorem. We also characterize all configurations for which the bound is attained. This is joint work with Jeck Lim and Skand Parvatikar.

title: Undoing Gender in French Literature
description: The French modernist canon has been read has a key site for sexual dissidence, but what about gender? In this talk, Mat Fournier presents his book, Dysphoric Modernism, and questions the entanglements of the modern gender binary with state power and colonial history. Through readings of Gide, Genet, Colette, and others, Fournier explores how narratives of sexual dissidence both deconstruct and reinforce mutually exclusive definitions of masculinity and femininity and racial discriminations. In this web of contradictions, modern gender appears as inherently dysphoric, imposing untenable positions and perpetuating systemic hierarchies. Ultimately, tracking the dysphoria traversing modernist writings offers a perspective into gender’s complicity with historical and contemporary fascisms, and offers strategies of resistance.

Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. description: We begin with a 10-15 minute warm-up consisting of fundamental dance techniques, specific hip hop technique, stretching, and cardio. Hip Hop Dance began at block parties in the Bronx in the 1970’s and drew from dance moves inspired by African Dance, Brazilian martial arts (Capoeira) and many Kung Fu movies. Bronx Rapper Afrika Bambaata drew from his experience watching African tribal dancing in creating the first group of hip hop dancers. DJ Kool Herc, inspired by his Jamaican roots, created the musical beats by spinning two records simultaneously. With many other influences along the way, Hip Hop has established itself as a dance form with a long history and vital and dynamic presence in our culture. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Sharon began dancing Hip Hop with Robin Tyler and her Funk girl group in Cambridge, MA. She went on to teach Hip Hop as part of her T.A. at Boston Conservatory, where she earned he MFA in Dance and wrote her thesis in Hip Hop history and evolution. She has performed and choreographed across the US: locally at The Dance Complex and Strand Theater, in NYC at WAXworks and HATCH Presenting Series at Jennifer Muller Works and Greenspace in Long Island City and internationally, including at Paris Music Festival and Disneyland Paris. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Reggaeton developed through a blend of Caribbean and Latin American influences, with roots in Panama and Puerto Rico and strong connections to reggae en español, dancehall, and hip-hop. Today, the genre has grown into a global cultural movement while remaining deeply connected to the Latin and Caribbean communities that shaped it. Since then, I have continued my training and recently earned the Senior Instructor designation, which allows me to teach across all levels of the method. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

title: The Fringe
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. title: Art + Science: Papermaking
description: Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join members of our Straus Center staff for an informal monthly conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, Penley Knipe, the Philip and Lynn Straus Senior Conservator of Works on Paper and head of the Paper Lab, will talk about the history of paper, including how it is made and what it can tell us about a work of art. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections.

title: Online Seminar On Undergraduate Mathematics Education
description: Speaker: Dan Meyer(Amplify) Title: Generative Questions About Generative AI in Math Learning Abstract: We are four years into the generative AI era and we can confidently say: (1) it is the most novel new technology of the last two decades, (2) it has fallen well short of expectations in education. Teacher usage remains lower than predicted. Schools operate identically now as years ago. Generative AI’s greatest contribution to education, so far, is the generation of important questions about the capacities of the technology, the needs of students, and the nature of teaching. title: Eleni Sikelianos and Julie Carr: the William Corbett Poetry Series
description: Born into a family of bohemians, poets, tree workers, ne’er-do-wells, visionaries, and smalltime sort-of hustlers, Eleni Sikelianos is a poet, writer, collaborator, and “master of mixing genres” (according to TimeOut). Kirkus has called her most recent book, Memory Rehearsal (City Lights, 2026; the third book in her trilogy of ancestral encounters) “a moving family memoir and a triumph of cultural archaeology.” Deeply engaged with ecopoetics, her work takes up urgent concerns of environmental precarity and ancestral lineages. Her tenth book of poetry, Your Kingdom came out in 2023. Her work has been translated into a dozen languages, and she has in turn translated works by Jacques Roubaud, Sabine Macher, and, most recently, Mohamed Leftah. She grew up in earshot of the ocean, in small coastal towns near Goleta, and has since lived in San Francisco, New York, Paris, Athens (Greece), Boulder (Colorado), and Providence. Julie Carr’s recent books are The Garden (Overflow, book one); Underscore; Mud, Blood, & Ghosts: Populism, Eugenics, & Spiritualism in the American West. Her co-translations of Leslie Kaplan’s Excess–The Factory and The Book of Skies, were published by Commune Editions & Pamenar Press. Books two and three of Overflow will be published sequentially over the next few years. She lives in Denver where she co-runs Counterpath, teaches at the University of Colorado Boulder, & hosts the podcast “Return the Key: Jewish Questions for Everyone.”

title: The Gilded Rose Book Bash with Joanna Shupe & Sarah MacLean
description: Join USA Today bestselling author Joanna Shupe for The Gilded Rose Book Bash, a celebration of an angst-filled, Beauty and the Beast inspired romance set amid the excess and opulence of Gilded Age New York. Caroline thought she was stepping into a fairy tale when she married Manhattan’s most sought-after bachelor, but behind closed doors, her marriage becomes a nightmare. When the chance to catalogue a private library gives her a lifeline, Caroline finds not only the literary treasures she’s been missing, but also Zane Bishop, a brilliant, wealthy recluse who understands her pain and is determined to help set her free. Come hear Shupe in conversation with bestselling author and romance champion Sarah MacLean as they talk about resilience, forbidden passion, complicated heroines, and the transformative power of love. Joanna will add personalizations to your pre-signed copies of The Gilded Rose as well as up to two of her titles brought from home. 6:30 PM: Doors Open – Grab your pre-signed book and a drink from the Lovestruck Bar & Cafe, settle in, and get ready for a great discussion! 7:00 PM: Discussion Begins – Joanna and Sarah will dive into The Gilded Rose. 7:45 PM: Q&A Session – Your chance to ask the author about their writing process! 8:00 PM: Signatures, Snapping Pics, and Salutations – Meet the author , and get your book personalized. 8:30 PM : Last call – Grab your final pour from the wine bar and head to the register for any book purchases. 9:00 PM: Event Wraps Up – Thanks for joining us!

title: Nondualism Trio presents Nosferatu Funk
description: $15 admission / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated & standing The Boston-based progressive jazz group Nondualism Trio presents "Nosferatu Funk" at the Lilypad! Featuring Mark Tipton (trumpet), James Heazlewood-Dale (bass), and Paul July Joseph (drums), Nondualism Trio will be playing original works, including Mark's compositions from their upcoming album, "Nosferatu Funk." The set will include: "Paraconsistent Refractions," "Walk-A-Seven Ghost Dance," "Lithospheric Waltz," "Cosmic Dust Groove Thang," "Into the Wilderness," "Slow Burn," "Nosferatu Funk," a pair of musical "Mantras," and more! Expect deep grooves, musical complexity, and synergistic ensemble playing. Nondualism Trio is a Boston-based progressive jazz trio that includes Mark Tipton on trumpet, James Heazlewood-Dale on bass, and Paul July Joseph on drums. Mark is originally from Maine, James is originally from Australia, and Paul is from Haiti. Nondualism Trio was formed in 2025 and in February 2026 they recorded their first album at Q Division Studios in Cambridge, MA, featuring Mark’s original compositions. They have recently performed at The Lilypad in Cambridge, The Drake in Amherst, and NEC’s Pierce Hall. The ensemble’s name, Nondualism Trio, is derived from the Indian philosophy that views reality as an interconnected whole, devoid of dualistic thinking, whereby awareness can be experienced beyond conceptual thought. It is this state of mind that Nondualism Trio seeks to embody when they are performing together: collectively open-minded in their improvisations to carry the music wherever it wants to go, and free from judgements and intuited mental road-blocks. Their music is both structured and open. The three members of Nondualism Trio are all rising talents in jazz, and are all active musicians on the Boston scene, seasoned touring musicians, and devoted teachers (Mark at NEC, James at Brandeis, and Paul through his private studio). title: Broadway Trivia
description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! The game will start at 7:30 pm, and is about two hours long (with plenty of beer breaks, of course). Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

My goal is to create a welcoming, judgment-free environment where students can get a great workout, build confidence, and most importantly, have fun dancing to music they love. Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Reggaeton developed through a blend of Caribbean and Latin American influences, with roots in Panama and Puerto Rico and strong connections to reggae en español, dancehall, and hip-hop. Today, the genre has grown into a global cultural movement while remaining deeply connected to the Latin and Caribbean communities that shaped it. I am a certified Senior Instructor with Latina Tribe, a dance fitness method focused on creating empowering spaces for women and members of the LGBTQ+ community. I began my journey with Latina Tribe as a student in 2021 and, after years of practicing the method, became a certified instructor and began teaching in 2024. Since then, I have continued my training and recently earned the Senior Instructor designation, which allows me to teach across all levels of the method. My main goal is to connect with every person that steps in my classes, creating a space where movement, fitness, community, and self-expression come together. I began my studies informally in 1997 while at Tufts University with Gretchenji and was hooked. From 2003 to 2011 I trained, taught, and toured as a member of the Chitresh Das Dance Company (CDDC) all across the US and India, holding lead roles such as Sita in Sita Haran. I have been steeped in this incredibly rich tradition of kathak, with it’s elements of dance, music, history, philosophy, math, and so much more and am thrilled to share with students and audiences widely in a manner that highlights how universal and accessible and FUN it really is! We encourage everyone to explore the history of this dance, the dancers that created it in Southern California, and the music and musicians that made it possible. Balboa today is an improvisational, joyful partner dance with a vibrant worldwide community, evolving into the present while honoring its origins. July and Stan have danced Balboa since the early 2000s, learning from original SoCal dancers and the second-generation teachers who came after them. description: Postpartum Movement is a welcoming, supportive space to move, reconnect, and care for yourself during the postpartum journey.
