Move at your own pace, take breaks whenever you need, and choose what feels right for you. Babies are warmly welcome, but you do not need to bring your baby to participate. No previous movement or yoga experience is needed. All bodies, all levels, and all postpartum experiences are welcome. Come as you are. Cost: $0 – $22 Sliding Scale REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. During this time, she earned her Prenatal Yoga Certification through OM Yoga

title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Cost: $20 Single Class | $15.00 barre | 5-class package $90.00 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

title: Screening of Presence
description: Join us for a midday screening exploring how public life has been staged, recorded, and remembered on screen. Presence is a film installation by Jingrong Zhang, supported by the Council for the Arts at MIT (CAMIT). Drawing on archival and cinematic footage across cultures and historical periods, the work assembles a "global supercut" of public gatherings: moments of solitude, chance encounters, street life, and collective assembly. As the montage builds from isolated figures to dense crowds, it invites viewers to consider how strangers come together in public space, and how those moments of shared presence have been captured on screen across a century of image-making. Every crowd on screen was once as present as we are now.

title: SCSB Colloquium with Dr. Jason Lerch: Towards Biologically Informed Subgroups Across Neurodevelopmental Disorders
description: Date: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Location: 46-3002 (Singleton Auditorium) Time: 4:00pm-5:00pm ET, followed by reception Speaker: Jason Lerch, Ph.D. Affiliation: Professor of Neuroscience, Oxford Centre for Integrative Neuroimaging, Nuffield Department of Clinical Neuroscience, University of Oxford Host: Dr. Alan Jasanoff Talk title: Towards Biologically Informed Subgroups Across Neurodevelopmental Disorders Abstract: Autism and related neurodevelopmental conditions are remarkably diverse, making it difficult to predict outcomes or identify effective treatments. In this talk, I will describe a translational neuroimaging approach that combines data from 135 mouse models (3,515 mice) with two human MRI cohorts (n = 1,234 and n = 1,015) to identify subgroups based on shared patterns of brain anatomy. Rather than reflecting conventional diagnoses such as autism, ADHD, or OCD, these subgroups appear to align with a small number of molecular pathways, including those involved in synaptic function, MAPK/Wnt signalling, chromatin regulation, and immune-related processes. These findings suggest that neurobiological subgroups may provide a useful framework for linking diverse clinical presentations to underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: Lie Groups Seminar
description: Speaker: Guy Shtotland (Ben-Gurion University) Title: Relative Kazhdan Lusztig isomorphism for GL2n\Sp2n Abstract: The Kazhdan–Lusztig isomorphism, which relates the affine Hecke algebra of a p-adic group to the equivariant K-theory of the Steinberg variety of its Langlands dual, played a key role in the proof of the Deligne–Langlands conjecture on the classification of tamely ramified irreducible representations. For a spherical variety X, we can construct two modules over the affine Hecke algebra: the first by considering Iwahori invariant functions on X, and the second using relative Langlands duality and equivariant K-theory. It is natural to expect a relationship between these modules. I will discuss this relationship for X = GL2n\Sp2n and its application to the study of distinguished representations.

title: Richard P. Stanley Seminar in Combinatorics
description: Speaker: Jonathan Boretsky (McGill) Title: Totally positive skew symmetric matrices Abstract: A matrix is totally positive if all of its minors are positive. The classical notion of total positivity coincides with the type A version of Lusztig’s more general total positivity in reductive real-split algebraic groups. Since skew-symmetric matrices always have nonpositive entries, they are not totally positive in the classical sense. The space of skew-symmetric matrices is an affine chart of the orthogonal Grassmannian OGr(n, 2n). Thus, we define a skew-symmetric matrix to be totally positive if it lies in the totally positive orthogonal Grassmannian. We provide a positivity criterion for these matrices in terms of a fixed collection of minors, and show that their Pfaffians have a remarkable sign pattern. The totally positive orthogonal Grassmannian is a CW cell complex and is subdivided into Richardson cells. We introduce a method to determine which cell a given point belongs to in terms of its associated matroid.

title: The Many Lives of Theban Tomb 16
description: The ancient Egyptian tomb known as Theban Tomb 16 dates to the reign of Ramesses II in the 19th Dynasty of the New Kingdom (around 1250 BCE). Originally, it served as the burial place of a priest named Panehsy and his wife, Tarenu, a chantress. Long after their lifetimes, the tomb remained an important resting place and was reused for more than a thousand years by members of the Theban elite. By the late 19th or early 20th century, the tomb had been looted, and it suffered further plundering in the 1970s. Since 2008, however, a team from the University of Memphis has been working to document and conserve both the tomb and its many secondary burials. In this program, Egyptologist Suzanne Onstine will present the latest research on the tomb’s beautifully painted plaster scenes, exploring what they reveal about life in ancient Egypt as well as funerary culture during the first millennium BCE. Free event parking is available with registration. Register by October 20 to receive parking registration instructions. Advance registration is recommended. Presented by the Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East in association with the Harvard Museums of Science & Culture. About the Speaker: Suzanne Onstine is an associate professor in the Department of History at the University of Memphis. She received her BA in Anthropology at the University of Arizona and her MA and PhD in Near and Middle Eastern Civilizations at the University of Toronto. She has conducted archaeological research in Egypt for thirty years and currently directs the University of Memphis mission to Theban Tomb 16 (TT16), the tomb of Panehsy in Dra Abu el-Naga, Luxor. She has published many works on women and religion in addition to various aspects of her research in TT16.

description: Experience the polar regions through the lens of photographer Leonard Sussman. What does it take to create a photograph at the edge of the world? From the Arctic to Antarctica and everywhere in between, his work captures some of Earth's most remote locations. Since 2014, Sussman has embarked on over a dozen expeditions to some of Earth's most remote and breathtaking locations: the Svalbard archipelago, Alaska, Greenland, Patagonia, Antarctica, and the sub-Antarctic islands of New Zealand and Australia. His camera has captured these fragile, stunning environments in ways that challenge and inspire. Sussman will share stunning imagery from his polar expeditions, reveal the challenges of photographing in extreme environments, and discuss his book, From Brooklyn to the North Pole: 52 Days on the USCG Icebreaker Healy. Copies of Sussman's book will be available for purchase following the event. A limited number of free tickets are available for full-time students with ID. Please reach out to museumregadmin@mit.edu. title: Beginner NY Salsa
description: Classes will be broken into 5 sections at Level 1. New sessions start the first Monday of every odd month. Warmup Footwork Review Foundational move for Level 1 On2 Linear Salsa (of which there are 7) Dance with Music Philosophically things to be on the lookout for, the importance of melding footwork and partner-work when dancing Salsa, the importance of spaced repetition, the importance of tying everything to Social dancing, and personal convolutional schemes to try to attenuate the lead/follow dichotomy. No partner required. *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. *Students who purchase a membership for the Dance Complex will get that $25 taken off their 10 class new student rate, bringing it down to $85. Cost: $23 Single Class | $85 for 5-Class Package | $130 for 10-Class Package | $110 for new student 10-class package Cash, Venmo (@Brendan-Folan), Zelle (bjfoley21@gmail.com) REGISTRATION: Not Required, Drop-Ins Welcome What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I was the assistant teacher of this class for over 2 years under Ricardo Contreras. title: Live Blues & Roots Music Returns to Harvard Square: Wednesday Nights @ The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar
description: The Sea Hag Restaurant & Bar and The Barrett Anderson Band are excited to announce a new weekly series, Blues & Roots Wednesdays , bringing live music back home to historic Harvard Square. “Cambridge, our fair city, and I share deep roots, and I’m thrilled to find a new musical home at The Sea Hag,” says Massachusetts-based singer/guitarist, Barrett Anderson. “Good music and good food are two of our most basic, fundamental needs,” he continues, “What great joy they give us. I am so happy to revel in that every Wednesday night with my dearest musical friends, and Kari and her incredible team at The Sea Hag. We go way back together, and I can’t imagine all the fun we have ahead.” Indeed, Anderson has strong connections to this scene. He remembers: “My first professional experience came when I was 15, backing up Muddy Waters’ band alums Pinetop Perkins and Bob Margolin at the original House of Blues on Winthrop Street. A few months after that I began busking, you’d often find me in Brattle Square or by the pit. This would have been mid/late 90s.” While still a teen, Anderson was a member of The Monster Mike Welch Band and Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters (“Ronnie was my guitar hero. Then he was my teacher, then my boss. Now he’s my musical Father,” Anderson says), before eventually starting The Barrett Anderson Band in 2007. Anderson won a Boston Music Award (2013 Blues Artist of the Year), was on the Billboard charts (2020’s live album Hynoboogie spent 3 weeks on the Billboard Blues Album chart, peaking at #6), and was nominated for a Blues Music Award (2023 Band of the Year with Anthony Geraci & The Boston Blues All-Stars), all the while playing nationally, internationally, and locally in Cambridge and the greater Boston area. In addition to the musical roots, long-time locals may recognize Anderson from a decade serving tables and bartending at The Sea Hag’s sister establishment, Grendel’s Den, or from Abodeon, the mid-century modern shop started by his family. title: Kenzō Tange Lecture: Maria Claudia Clemente and Francesco Isidori “The Architecture of Public Space”
description: Today, approximately 56% of the world’s population—equivalent to 4.7 billion people—live in urban areas, and that number is constantly growing. This phenomenon of unchecked growth, evident in both global megacities and “old” European cities, has led to the pulverization of the very concept of the city. In this context, the public space around which Europe’s great cities were built—the space of thecivitas, major collective events and street demonstrations, as well as, more simply, the place where one encounters the “other”—seems to be vanishing, giving way to a void of quality and identity. To bring public space back to the center of the debate, we must reflect on a different vision of the city, one structured around the form of public space, that architecture can help shape and enrich. Drawing on the reflections inThe Architecture of Public Space(Park Books, 2023), the lecture will illustrate several examples from Labics’s recent architectural work, where the connection between architecture, the city, and public space is most evident.

description: Special Live Event! It’s been ten years, and we can still remember the fresh podcast. The recording equipment had never been used. The movies had never been watched. The Bechdel Cast was called “The Show of Dreams”… and it was, it really was! Join hosts Jamie Loftus and Caitlin Durante for a LIVE SHOW celebrating their TEN YEAR ANNIVERSARY of hosting The Bechdel Cast! Caitlin and Jamie are taking a look at the past decade of (genius, brilliant, important) discussions about film, and pondering how releasing radical mp3s every week didn’t fix global misogyny! It will be a spectacular, full of videos, games, fan fic, Shrek references (Shreferences), you name it! It’s Halloween season, so come dressed as a movie character, because you bet your ass Jamie and Caitlin will be in costume! SEE YOU THERE! Tickets for this special event are $35. No Brattle passes will be accepted.

title: Dance Sassy with Chris
description: Students can expect a welcoming, all-levels class that begins with a warm-up, followed by step-by-step choreography, time to dance the full routine, and a cooldown. Each class is designed so beginners can focus on the core movement while more experienced dancers can add styling, texture, and performance. Chris’s teaching philosophy centers on clarity, encouragement, and creating a supportive space where every dancer can build confidence and enjoy expressing themselves. Cost: $22.85 Single Class ($20 class + 2.85 Eventbrite processing fees) *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Eventbrite Registration What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Dance Sassy is an open-style choreography class inspired by the energy of pop music videos, K-pop performances, and styles such as hip hop, jazz-funk, and fem-style dance. More than learning steps, the class is about moving for joy, expressing your personality, and building confidence in a supportive community. It gives dancers space to let go of everyday stress, embrace their own style, and feel powerful through movement. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Chris began dancing in 2007, finding joy, confidence, and self-expression through pop and K-pop choreography. He began teaching cardio dance at fitness centers in Indonesia in 2011 and has continued developing his practice through years of teaching, performing, and creating accessible choreography, including as a Dance Complex teaching artist since 2014. Dance Sassy is his own open-style approach, drawing inspiration from pop performance, jazz-funk, hip hop, and K-pop while prioritizing clear, step-by-step instruction. title: Chair Yoga with Nora Stephens
description: Chair Yoga is a welcoming, accessible movement practice designed to make the benefits of yoga available to every body. Using a chair for support, we’ll explore gentle movement, stretching, breath, and balance to support strength, mobility, flexibility, and greater ease in the body. Movements can be adapted to meet you where you are, whether you’re new to yoga, returning to movement, or looking for a practice that doesn’t require getting down on the floor. Move at your own pace, take breaks whenever you need, and choose what feels right for your body. No need to get down on the floor. All bodies and all levels are welcome. No previous yoga experience is needed. Cost: $0 – $22 Sliding Scale REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. title: Walking Tour: Reading the Urban Landscape
description: This event is at capacity. Join us for a special gallery talk that includes a walking tour! Graduate student teacher Ryan Schmidt-Knapik will first discuss the exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors in the galleries before leading a walking tour on campus, where you will learn how to interpret and appreciate nature in our urban landscape. We will focus on exploring how humans shape the ecology of urban landscapes and how plants in these ecosystems in turn shape our relationship with nature. Led by: Ryan Schmidt-Knapik, Graduate student teacher and Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, Harvard University On Location: Drawing the Outdoors features drawings by J. M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. The catalogue was made possible by the Andrew W. Mellon Publication Funds. Additional project support was provided by the Almathea Charitable Foundation.

title: Somatic Movement with Mariah Sabir
description: Somatic Movement is a welcoming space to slow down, reconnect with your body, and explore movement from the inside out. Through grounding, breath, gentle movement, rest, and moments of stillness, you’ll be invited to notice what your body needs and move in ways that feel supportive to you. Rather than focusing on how movement looks, this practice centers how it feels—creating space to release tension, support nervous system regulation, and build greater connection with yourself. Each class explores themes such as boundaries, self-trust, rest, joy, transition, and community. There is no right way to move and nothing to achieve. You are always encouraged to listen to your body, move at your own pace, and make the practice your own. All bodies and all levels are welcome. title: Symplectic Geometry Seminar
description: Dylan Cant (Université de Montréal) Title: On the spectral diameter of the Grassmannians Abstract: For a compact symplectic manifold 𝑀 there is a spectral pseudometric on the universal cover of 𝐻𝑎𝑚(𝑀), built from Floer theory. A folklore conjecture says its diameter should be infinite whenever the symplectic form vanishes on 𝑝𝑖2(𝑀), on the other hand the presence of symplectic spheres can force the diameter to be finite, as happens for 𝐶𝑃𝑛. I will discuss what happens for the complex Grassmannians 𝐺𝑟(𝑘, 𝑛). We show that the spectral diam- eter of 𝐺𝑟(2, 𝑛) is finite when 𝑛 is prime, and that the spectral diameter of 𝐺𝑟(2𝑘, 2𝑛) is infinite when 𝑘 < 𝑛 (both over a field of characteristic zero; in nonzero characteristic there is a more refined statement for 𝐺𝑟(2, 𝑛)). The finiteness comes from the quantum cohomology of the Grassmannian, and the infiniteness comes from Lagrangian submanifolds. This is joint work with Habib Alizadeh, Marcelo Atallah and Jianqiao Shang.

title: Music Forum: Makoto Takao
description: Thursday, October 22nd at 5pm Lewis Music Library Please join us for a light reception in the Lewis Music Library after the event. The King’s Singing Orphans: Music, Mission, and Japan’s Hidden Christians What do a sixteenth-century Marian hymn, a fishing island off Nagasaki, and UNESCO have in common? In 1551, a group of orphaned boys boarded a ship in Lisbon. Chosen for the quality of their voices, they were dispatched by King João III along the trade routes of the Portuguese Empire. Traveling through Mozambique, Goa, and Malacca, two of them eventually landed on the shores of southern Japan in 1556, carrying Catholic song into a country that would soon outlaw Christianity altogether. Four and a half centuries later, on the small island of Ikitsuki, the last descendants of Japan’s “hidden Christians” still chant prayers whose words no longer belong to any singular language and whose melodies sound, to the casual ear, like Buddhist sutra. In 2018, UNESCO recognized their villages and churches as World Heritage sites, but not the endangered oral traditions kept alive within them. This talk follows the global lives of the king’s singing orphans to ask what connects these two worlds and what we stand to lose if we fail to listen before the singing stops. About the Speaker Makoto Harris Takao is an Assistant Professor of Music and the Class of 1957 Career Development Professor at MIT. Working at the intersection of cultural history, religious studies, and musicology, Takao maps Japan’s entanglement with other world regions over the past 500 years. His current book project, The Clef and the Cross: Music and Kirishitan Transculturation in Sixteenth-Century Japan, asks what early modern Japanese Catholicism sounded like and how it was understood and expressed through Buddhist frameworks of sound, music, and movement. His work to date has appeared in such venues as Early Music, Journal of Music History Pedagogy, Journal of Religious History, Journal of Jesuit Studies, Zeit

title: Artist Talk: Hao Jingban
description: The List Visual Arts Center will host an artist talk in celebration of the opening of Hao Jingban: I Witness followed by an opening reception. Artist, Hao Jingban, will be in conversation with doctoral student in East Asian Film and Media Studies at Harvard University, Huirong Ye. This exhibition marks Hao’s first major US museum solo, featuring recent work centered on I Witness (2025), a three-channel installation that takes up the embodied residue of the COVID-19 pandemic: four participants move slowly through a well-lit apartment, their images punctuated by stories of loss—an older woman who sleeps alone and rises to clean her refrigerator, a group of young people pacing an open field. Hao Jingban lives and works between Yunnan Province, China, and Berlin, Germany. She received an MA from the University of London and BA from Goldsmiths College. Recent solo exhibitions include Mori Art Museum, Tokyo (2025); Matadero Madrid (2020); OCT Contemporary Art Terminal, Xi’an, China (2019) and recent group exhibitions at venues including 36th Bienal de São Paulo (2025); Rockbund Art Museum (2025); TANK Shanghai (2024); West Bund Museum, Shanghai (2023); Seoul Mediacity Biennale (2021); among others. Hao’s works are in the collection of the M+, Hong Kong; Centre Pompidou, Paris; Frac Bretagne, Rennes; the Power Station of Art, Shanghai;, Museu d’Art Contemporani de Barcelona, Barcelona. Huirong Ye is a doctoral student in East Asian Film and Media Studies at Harvard University. Her current research examines the archivalization and institutionalization of meteorology in modern China, focusing on how it became configured as a mediated domain through audiovisual, technological, textual, and spatial forces, where visibility, legibility, and manageability operate as ideals within evolving regimes of prediction. Her broader interests include environmental humanities, transpacific island and ocean studies, sensory history, activist media, and contemporary art. Huirong holds a BA i

title: Carrie McKnelly
description: Carrie McKnelly Part of the MIT Fall 2026 Architecture Lecture Series. Presented with the Design and Computation Group Carrie McKnelly is a design leader whose work sits at the intersection of computational design and material craft. She leads the design team within Nike Innovation's Advanced Digital Creation Studio, spanning footwear, apparel, and accessories, directing digital workflows that embed performance, behavior, and data into how product is imagined, designed, and made. Carrie holds a Master of Science in Architectural Studies from MIT, studied through the Computation and Design Group, and a Bachelor of Architecture from Pratt Institute. She has taught studio and elective courses at MIT and Pratt, and served as the Howard E. LeFevre Emerging Practitioner Fellow at Ohio State's Knowlton School of Architecture (2015–2016). Carrie began her career at SOFTlab in New York, designing large-scale installations that revealed the creative potential of pairing computational logic with physical material. At MIT, she explored knit textiles as a material system for complex form and worked alongside the Self-Assembly Lab. She then joined Nike, leading computational design across products including DriFit Advanced for the 2024 Paris Olympics and Athlete Imagined Revolutions, thirteen concepts co-created with athletes and generative AI. In her current role, she shapes the future of product design through emerging technologies, energized by where computational design and material craft will evolve next. This lecture will be held in person in the Sidara Auditorium (W41- 1216) and streamed online on YouTube. Lectures are free and open to the public. Registration is required.

title: 2026 Fall Exhibitions Opening Reception
description: Join us for the opening reception to celebrate two new exhibitions at the List Center: Uri Aran: Look How Hard They Work and Hao Jingban: I Witness. The opening reception will follow an Artist Talk with exhibiting artist, Hao Jingban, from 5:30-6:30PM. Exhibiting artists and exhibition curators will be in attendance. Light refreshments and beverages from Momma's Grocery + Wine will be served. Uri Aran: Look How Hard They Work Uri Aran's work is at once deeply idiosyncratic and oddly familiar: to follow it is to tinker alongside the artist, to be let in on an invention, or perhaps a shorthand between friends. Aran’s first major institutional solo exhibition in the United States gathers a new body of work: annotated panels that hover between quick line drawing and painting, welded sculptures that pose like equations, bulbous forms worked by hand in plasticene and foam, and a mass of piled-up googly eyes—the most elementary form of affect and animation—tragicomically raised to the scale of an earthwork. Hao Jingban: I Witness Blending documentary sensibility with poetic construction, Hao Jingban makes moving-image installations that are emotionally precise, historically incisive, and formally experimental. Hao’s first major US museum solo gathers recent work centered on I Witness (2025), a three-channel installation that takes up the embodied residue of the COVID-19 pandemic: four participants move slowly through a well-lit apartment, their images punctuated by stories of loss—an older woman who sleeps alone and rises to clean her refrigerator, a group of young people pacing an open field.

title: Tap Level 2
description: Carrying on the tradition of Boston Tap, established by Maureen Cosgrove in 1976, these classes focus on developing technique, rhythm and musicality. Prior tap experience is recommended for Level 2 (Intermediate). Classes are workshop format, typically 7-week sessions. Each class will build on the weeks before, but students may join at any time if space allows. Written notation for set warm-ups are available for those who are interested. New 7-week tap session 9/10 – 10/22 Cost: $20 single class | 7 week session $120 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. REGISTRATION: Email selapbailey@gmail.com Pre-registration required. Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, PayPal, Credit Card, Apple Pay (email selapbailey@gmail.com for payment information) What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Tap is an American dance form in which rhythms are audibly tapped out on the floor. It has origins in slavery and the percussive dances of West African Juba dance and Irish step dancing. It developed through minstrel shows and vaudeville in the late 19th century and emerged along with jazz in the 20th century into the art form we know today. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Sela has been a tap teacher since 2000, taking over Maureen Cosgrove’s Boston Tap classes at the Dance Complex in 2014. While at Smith College she studied in the Five College Dance Department, performing with the Celebrations Dance Company and the UMass University Dancers. She was a founding member of the Terpsichore Ensemble in Amherst, MA and taught tap classes in Amherst and Northampton, MA before moving to Boston. Sela teaches adult beginner and intermediate tap classes at the Dance Complex, and made her Dance Complex choreographic debut at the 2018 Spring Teaching Artists and Student Concert with students from the intermediate tap class. title: Skip the Small Talk Night Online
description: Meaningful online conversations with strangers on Zoom that don't leave you drained. We use question prompts to spark unique convos. You may expect this event to run from 7:00 - 8:15pm ET/ 6:00 - 7:15 pm CT/ 5:00 - 6:15 pm MT/ 4:00 - 5:15 pm PT. Please be aware of time zone differences. About this event ***You'll need the event URL, so be sure to register in advance so we can send it to you. We'll send you an e-mail with the Zoom link a few minutes after you purchase a ticket (and we’ll also send it again the day of the event)-- please check both your “spam” AND “junk” folders if you don't see it!*** ---- These Zoom events are designed based in psychology research to give you all the warm fuzzy feelings of human closeness, without that feeling of Zoom-fatigue afterward. We use question prompts and a structure designed based in psychology research to help you get vulnerable with strangers in a way that actually feels safe, and that brings out the best in people. All our events are trauma-informed and facilitated by folks with therapeutic training. According to our surveys, a lot of our guests report feeling nervous about coming, but 100% of the people who say they were nervous also end up saying they were glad they came. There might be some selection bias going on, but we still think it's promising :) We even had an academic paper come out about our online events showing that they improve mood and reduce loneliness! Check that out here: https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5827683e6a49634bd84b79f4/t/614cfad6e033d105a07cc40f/1632434903586/preprint-28002-submitted.pdf What's it like? The whole thing is on Zoom. We'll put you into pairs in breakout rooms, and you'll switch partners so you're not just talking to the same person the whole night. We'll give you question prompts to spark conversations to make sure you're getting the most out of your conversations. title: ONELOUDDRAWING
description: ONELOUDDRAWING Jonah / onelinedrawing with a full band doing Far’s Tin Cans on its 30th anniversary, plust stuff from New End’s Thriller & the new onelinedrawing album RAINBOWMACHINE ARTIST BIO: onelinedrawing is Jonah Matranga of Far, Gratitude, New End Original, and more. On September 18, Iodine Recordings will release RAINBOWMACHINE, the new album from onelinedrawing. The album was produced by Jay Maas. It’s the loudest, wildest onelinedrawing record yet. The tracks above are from the album. There will also be the first full-band onelinedrawing shows in forever in September and October, celebrating the 30th anniversary of Far’s TIn Cans With Strings To You, the 25th anniversary of Thriller, and of course the new album. Jonah started onelinedrawing in 1998, just as his first band, post-hardcore / emo misfits Far, was breaking up. The first onelinedrawing releases were a cassette on POPROCKIT, a label started by Kevin Seconds (7 Seconds). Then came the Sketchy EPs, first self-released, then in various forms on various indie labels (Crank, Revelation, Corrupted Image). During that time, onelinedrawing pioneered sliding-scale pricing for downloads and merch, monthly crowdfunded patronage (eventually released as the Always New albums), and Unique Recordings. During that time, onelinedrawing toured with and/or released music with Rival Schools, The Juliana Theory, Coheed & Cambria, Dashboard Confessional, Murder By Death, The Weakerthans, Jimmy Eat World, and more. onelinedrawing’s most recent studio album is Tenderwild, on Iodine Records. Iodine also recently released Sketchbook, a collection of early onelinedrawing recordings 1999-2001. onelinedrawing also has two albums (VISITOR and THE VOLUNTEERS) still on Jade Tree / Epitaph. Over 30 years, several projects, dozens of albums, hundreds of songs, and thousands of shows, Jonah Matranga has influenced countless artists: Deftones, Frank Turner, Thursday, My Chemical Romance, Walter Schreifels, and Chris Carraba. Jonah

description: Start adding some flavor to your dancing. This class reviews cross-body lead and covers inside turn and half right turn combining them with basic right and left turns. Salsa is a musical and dance style that originated in Cuba with African roots and European influences. It later developed in New York and it’s popular throughout Latin America in places like Puerto Rico, Colombia, Peru and Cuba just to name a few. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I grew up listening to Salsa music and later got interested in the dance. As a teenager, I was part of a Colombian folk dance group before starting to perform Salsa duets with my brother Andres. I’ve been teaching Salsa for about 27 years now and this year we are celebrating 23 years of our dance company, Salsa y Control. Finish this statement: I am passionate about teaching this style because… It allows people to connect in a unique way. Salsa dancing is a social dance that help break barriers and brings people together from all walks of life. It also gives you the opportunity to express yourself freely on the dance floor or stage. How can students learn more about this offering? This album features Lyle Lovett, Hayes Carll, Susan Gibson, Darden Smith, Shake Russell and more. It takes listeners on a stirring musical journey across genres from Folk and Rock to Country and Americana. Charting #7 on Folk Chart & #9 on Alt Country Radio Charts. Central to Cooper's unique artistry is his ability to connect with audiences through his authentic stories, sense of humor and warm stage presence. The studio band consisting of legendary players -"The Section" with Leland Sklar & Russ Kunkel AKA "The Immediate Family." Since then, he worked with Shake Russell in Texas, releasing several albums together and performing on "Austin City Limits." Dana has also collaborated with several established artists - Kim Carnes (Betty Davis Eye's), Don Henry, Hal Ketchum, Kim Richey, Tom Kimmel & more. His 2022 CD "I Can Face The Truth" garnered much praise and attention, charting on 5 different Radio Charts. "Dana has a poet's eye for beauty & detail, a blue's man's soul and a songbird's gift. He is remarkable." - Hayes Carll Louis

title: Intermediate House
description: The Intermediate House class is for students who have learned basic house concepts/vocabulary and/or are comfortable learning independently in dance class. Intermediate House will expand upon the students’ understanding of step variations, freestyle concepts, musicality and body awareness at a faster pace than the beginner and open level classes. This class will challenge students’ physicality and understanding of music and movement. Come to class with an open mind and a comfortable pair of clean shoes. REGISTER HERE Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@sean-bjerke), Paypal/Zelle ( beejerks@gmail.com ), Credit Card through Pre-registration What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? One of the world’s most popular music genres, “house” is an electronic dance music genre that emerged in Chicago in the late 70s/early 80s following the disco era. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? A master Taekwondo-ist and professional dancer, Sean began dancing in the year 2000, and was formally introduced to house dance by Boston native Ricardo Foster Jr in 2007. description: Enjoy exercising in nature in this Outdoor Eastern Flow class! Connect mind, body, and spirit while getting into a state of Flow. title: Hourly Tour
description: Entrance to the historic house is by guided tour only, and all tours are free of charge. What does this house reveal about our shared past? Highlighting the house and its remarkable collections (original to the Longfellow period), this conversational tour will explore links between colonial-era slavery and freedom, Washington’s headquarters at the start of the American Revolution, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow’s poetic legacy, and the Longfellow family’s legacy of historic preservation.

title: The MIT AgeLab's Aging and Equity Speaker Series featuring Dr. Choi presenting "Too Hot for the Aging Brain? How Outdoor Heat May Shape Cognitive Aging and Dementia Risk"
description: Extreme heat is an increasingly common environmental stressor, yet its implications for brain aging remain poorly understood. In this seminar, Dr. Choi will present a program of research examining how outdoor heat exposure may contribute to brain health in later life. Drawing on nationally representative longitudinal data from older U.S. adults, Dr. Choi will discuss findings across multiple stages of the brain-aging continuum, from changes in cognitive function and incident dementia to blood-based biomarkers of neurodegeneration and Alzheimer’s disease-related pathology. Dr. Choi will also highlight potential sources of heterogeneity in vulnerability. Together, these studies illustrate how environmental exposures can be integrated into research on the biological and social determinants of brain aging and point to emerging questions about the implications of more frequent hot days for population aging. Eun Young Choi, PhD, is an Assistant Professor in the School of Social Work at Arizona State University. A gerontologist by training, she studies how the places we live shape how we age and why some populations face greater risks than others. Her work connects social and biological perspectives to examine how environmental stressors may influence brain health and dementia risk. Her research program has been supported by the National Institute on Aging and the Alzheimer’s Association. Her work has been featured by major news outlets, including The New York Times and NPR. She earned her PhD in Gerontology from the University of Southern California and completed postdoctoral training at New York University’s School of Global Public Health and the USC/UCLA Center on Biodemography and Population Health.

title: Hottel Lecture: Building a Sustainable, Circular, and Low-Carbon Chemical Industry
description: Speaker: Dionisios G. Vlachos, Unidel Dan Rich Chair in Energy Professor of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering; Director, Catalysis Center for Energy Innovation (CCEI); Director, Delaware Energy Institute (DEI); University of Delaware Dionisios (Dion) G. Vlachos is the Unidel Dan Rich Energy Chaired Professor of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering and Physics and Astronomy at the University of Delaware, where he also serves as Director of the Delaware Energy Institute (DEI). From 2009 to 2024, he directed the Catalysis Center for Energy Innovation (CCEI), an Energy Frontier Research Center funded by the Department of Energy. Vlachos received his five-year diploma in Chemical Engineering from the National Technical University of Athens in 1987, followed by his M.S. and Ph.D. from the University of Minnesota in 1990 and 1992, and a postdoctoral appointment at Minnesota's Army High-Performance Computing Research Center. He began his academic career at the University of Massachusetts in 1993, was promoted to associate professor in 1998, and joined the University of Delaware in 2000. Over his career, he has held visiting appointments at Princeton University (spring 2000), Thomas Jefferson University and Hospital (spring 2007), the University of Minnesota as the George Pierce Distinguished Professor (fall 2007), and EPFL (fall 2022). At Delaware, he held the Elizabeth Inez Kelley Professorship (2009–2016) and the Allan and Myra Ferguson Professorship (2016–2020) before assuming his current endowed chair. His research spans circular economy and waste valorization, multiscale modeling and simulation, process intensification and electrification, renewable fuels and chemicals, in silico materials prediction, and kinetic modeling. He is widely recognized as a pioneer in multiscale modeling and in foundational research on biomass conversion, plastics recycling, and upcycling. Vlachos has been recognized with numerous honors, including the Neal R. Amundson Life Achievement Awar

title: What Are People For: Design Philosophy by Patrick Whitney
description: What Are People For: Design Philosophy by Patrick Whitney Boston-Cambridge Premiere of Gary Hustwit’s New Film and Interactive Design Workshop Join the Morningside Academy of Design for the Boston-Cambridge Premiere of What Are People For: Design Philosophy by Patrick Whitney, the latest short film by acclaimed design documentarian Gary Hutwit (Helvetica, Objectified, Urbanized, Eno), and interactive design workshop on October 24th. Explore how design can address today's most complex challenges from 2-5pm with a hands-on workshop led by Evan Chan and André Nogueira. Chan and Nogueira will introduce the Whole View model, a systems design approach for reframing problems, surfacing the perspectives of diverse stakeholders, and finding new pathways forward in situations where expertise is abundant but fragmented. The session is designed for cross-sector leaders grappling with problems too complex for any one discipline to solve alone. The workshop will be followed by a screening at 5:30pm of What Are People For. The film is part of a larger multimedia project celebrating the life and work of Patrick Whitney, a pioneering figure in applying design to complex systemic challenges. Whitney's influence on the field has been profound, even as much of his work happened out of the spotlight. This project, produced by Murmur Ring with Ashley Lukasik and André Nogueira, offers a rare opportunity to engage directly with his ideas. Following the screening, a short panel conversation will start at 6pm, bringing the filmmakers and Patrick together to discuss design's expanding role in addressing complexity. This is a conversation built for a broad audience, regardless of prior design background. The evening will close with a reception, offering time to connect with fellow participants and the project team over refreshments. Together, the workshop, screening, and conversation create a shared foundation for dialogue and collaboration, inaugurating MAD's role as a convening space for sy

title: National Prescription Drug Take Back Day (220 Washington St.)
description: Somerville residents can participate in National Prescription Drug Take Back Day at two City staffed drop-off locations to safely dispose of expired or unused prescription medication. Staff from Somerville’s Community, Help, Outreach, and Recovery (COHR) unit of Somerville Police Department and the City’s Prevention Services division will also be onsite to provide prevention information and resources including free Narcan and fentanyl test strips. Drop off or stop by at two locations from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.: Public Safety Headquarters at 220 Washington Street Teele Square Fire Station at 6 Newbury St. For bottled medications, residents should remove or scratch out any personal information while leaving the name of the medication visible before disposing. Please make sure caps to liquid medications are secure. Year-round drop-off location: In addition to this event, Somerville offers 24/7, year-round disposal for unneeded prescription medications at the Somerville Public Safety Building (220 Washington Street). For more information, please contact 311 (617-666-3311).

title: C’port Textile & Book Drive, Oct. 24
description: ANNUAL TEXTILE/BOOK/VIDEO GAME DRIVE Sponsored by Cambridgeport Neighborhood Association (CAN) Clean Your Shelves; Reduce Waste; Help Non-Profits 10am to 2pm, October 24, 2026, in Hastings Square (corner of Brookline & Chestnut) Keep things out of landfills! Get your stuff to people who need it! Support the! Meet your neighbors! Bring all your unwanted, old, beat-up, or shelf-hogging books (as well as video games, DVDs, and CDs in their cases). It all will be taken by Bay State Books which supports Literacy projects such as The Prison Book program, Operation Paperback, and many friends of the library groups throughout Massachusetts. But that’s not all! For textiles, bring anything you can wear, sleep in, or dry yourself off with regardless of condition (torn, worn, stained, missing buttons, broken zippers, etc.)! This includes any type of material composed of natural or synthetic fibers, such as products made from wool, silk, linen, cotton, polyester, leather, vinyl, hemp, and rayon. But that’s still not all! In addition, Helpsy takes belts, ties, handkerchiefs, bandanas, wallets, purses, backpacks, totes, footwear, bedding and covers, halloween costumes, curtains, drapes, fabric shades, shower curtains, placemats, tablecloths, throw rugs, fabric mats, and even stuffed animals. The only requirement is that it be clean, dry, and odorless and loaded in bags or boxes. The textiles will be directly loaded in an electric truck run by Helpsy -- a Public Benefit (“B) Corporation whose mission is to keep clothes out of the trash and to create honorable work. In 2025 alone, Hepsy collected over 32 million pounds of clothes, shoes, and other items, 95% of what were reused or recycled.

description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk; space is limited. Fee: This is a free event. Accessibility accommodations: If you would like to request accommodations for your visit, please contact Visitor Services at am_register@harvard.edu or 617-495-9400. For more details about accommodations at the museums, please see the Accessibility page. General info: The museum visit page has general guidelines for your visit. On this tour, Priya Allen ’27 will explore the design and politics of historical drinking vessels and containers. The stops on the tour are a Persian jug from the 9th–10th century; a British abolition jug (c. 1810–20); and a samovar designed by Marianne Brandt in the Bauhaus metal workshop in Germany in 1925. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

description: Classes teach Broadway style tap and focus on repetitive technique to encourage muscle memory and the confidence to create clear sounds. Inclusion is a priority so that all students feel welcome. Classes are “drop-in”, meaning you may join any week and there’s no “semester” commitment. Past steps are always reviewed with the introduction of 1 or 2 new steps or combos each class. Similar to a yoga class, students work at their own individual levels and build up skill at their own pace. Beginners will feel comfortable regardless of when they join. Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@christina-harrington-7) What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. description: A guided improvisational movement practice that engages somatic awareness to facilitate personal growth, emotional well-being, and collective healing. Through verbal instructions, participants are invited to explore, in their own bodies way – a variety of movement patterns, physical inquiries, and focal points. The journey is curated to an intentional and eclectic world music soundscape. It is a journey where you might sweat (though you are always in control of your rhythm and pace).This class allows you to engage with the wisdom of your own body, to take you on a journey. This is a trauma-informed practice and container. GUIDELINES: Be on time PREPARATION: Wear clothing you can freely move and sweat in. Have water. title: Spotlight Tour: Disavowed, with Julianne Wu ’28
description: On this tour, Julianne Wu ’28 will look at instances of disavowal in three works that illuminate, disturb, or challenge authority, including Bearded Man, Possibly Emperor Macrinus (Roman, early to mid-3rd century CE), Max Beckmann’s Self-Portrait in Tuxedo (1927), and High Street (1950) by Franz Kline. Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. Open to the public, these tours start outside the museum shop on Saturdays and Sundays at 11am and 2pm. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram @harvardarthappens.

title: 250th Deep Dive Tour: Headquarters of a Revolution
description: Entrance to the historic house is by guided tour only, and all tours are free of charge. General George Washington’s Cambridge headquarters was a testing ground for many of the ideals, institutions, and questions that still define our nation. This conversational tour explores Cambridge Headquarters as a hub of revolutionary activity, where generals, enslaved people, paid laborers, poets, Indigenous diplomats, politicians, and soldiers shaped history - and how later generations would shape its memory.

title: Dafnis Prieto Sí o Sí Quartet
description: PERSONNEL: Dafnis Prieto, Drums, Compositions, Music Director Peter Apfelbaum, Soprano Sax, Tenor Sax, Flute Martin Bejerano, Piano Ricky Rodríguez, Electric Bass 25 years after his arrival in New York, the GRAMMY-winning and Latin GRAMMY-nominated drummer, composer, and MacArthur Fellow Dafnis Prieto has utterly shifted the sonic landscape of the jazz and creative music scene. With Prieto’s appearance on the NYC jazz scene likened to “an asteroid hitting the city” (The New York Times), and a reputation that rightfully lauds him as “one of the most multidimensional artists working today” (JazzTimes), the Cuban drummer strikes once again with his 10th album, 3 Sides of the Coin. This album marks the studio return of Prieto’s acclaimed Sí o Sí (“Yes or Yes”) Quartet, a rightfully jubilant cohort comprising Peter Apfelbaum on woodwinds, Martin Bejerano on piano, and Ricky Rodríguez on electric bass, brought together to commemorate both the bandleader’s quarter century in the United States and his 50th birthday.

title: Walk to End Alzheimer's - Greater Boston
description: The Alzheimer's Association invites the community to join the Greater Boston Walk to End Alzheimer's on October 25, 2026, at DCR Richard McKinnon Park in Cambridge. The Walk is the world's largest event dedicated to raising awareness and funds for Alzheimer's care, support, and research. More than 7 million Americans are living with Alzheimer's, and nearly 12 million family members and friends provide unpaid care for loved ones living with the disease. Funds raised through the Walk help the Alzheimer's Association advance critical research efforts while providing free support, education, and resources to families facing Alzheimer's and other dementias. The Greater Boston Walk brings together individuals, families, caregivers, community organizations, and corporate teams who are united in the fight against Alzheimer's and all other dementia. Participants of all ages are welcome and can register as individuals or as part of a team. As part of the event, participants are invited to take part in the Promise Garden ceremony, a moving tribute that honors those impacted by Alzheimer's and other dementias. Each flower in the Promise Garden represents a personal connection to the disease and serves as a powerful symbol of hope and determination. This year, the Walk to End Alzheimer's - Greater Boston is expected to have about 5,000 participants and participants are working together toward a fundraising goal of raising $2 million to support the Alzheimer's Association's mission. Those interested in joining the movement can register, donate, or learn more at act.alz.org/GreaterBoston.

As you travel along Indian Ridge, participants will be prompted to mindfully take in the autumn views, allowing the falling foliage to inspire you to: let go . Letting go of what is not serving us and what is out of our control is the goal. As you arrive at the green along Auburn lake, chairs will be set up for a chair yoga class. The chair allows a great view to gaze upon the lake as Lonnie guides participants through this moving meditation. The class will center generous exhales and prompt you to release unnecessary tension in the body and mind. The return walk to the chapel provides opportunity for reflection, considering what small practice could stay with you and remind you to let go . Please note that this workshop will meet at and return to Story Chapel. … Lonnie has taught chair yoga for 9 years weekly. Throughout their 30s as an active dancer, she has felt the benefits of this gentle practice and feels it is beneficial for many ages and mobilities. A note from Lonnie : “As a past artist in residence who choreographed a dance tour around Auburn Lake, I grew to know this corner of the cemetery quite well. It feels like a second home. I am thrilled for the opportunity to return and share my love of this path with others. Autumn is such a stunning time in New England. I hope for many to join me in taking in the site and allowing yourself some focused time to join the trees in a seasonal release.” REGISTER HERE>> Experience a deeper connection to Mount Auburn Cemetery with free or discounted access to all our public programs and special events by joining the Friends of Mount Auburn

title: Emissary Quartet: [moment]um
description: $20 admission / $10 for students / 5pm doors / 5:30 show Emissary Quartet’s debut album and concert program, [moment]um, is inspired by the Japanese concept of jo-ha-kyū , a structure that reflects the natural flow of progression: beginning slowly ( jo ), accelerating through development ( ha ), and culminating in a swift and powerful conclusion ( kyū ). This theme of movement, time, and motion is brought to life through contemporary works by living composers, Jennifer Higdon, Kai-Young Chan, Sung-Hyun Yun, Nicky Sohn, Heike Beckmann, and Herman Beeftink. Each composer uses the unique textures and timbres of the flute and auxiliary flutes, to evoke a sense of continuous transformation. Each piece within the album highlights various facets of moments and motion, from the meditative, gradually unfolding soundscapes of the opening movements to the more dynamic, rhythmically intricate passages that create a palpable sense of urgency and energy. The living composers draw upon a wide range of influences, blending minimalist repetition with more expansive, lyrical phrasing to reflect [moment]um , while exploring the capacity of sound to depict both literal and abstract forms of motion. Emissary Quartet is committed to cultivating connection and opportunity through dynamic performances and residencies that empower musicians and foster community. EQ has presented at various conventions, including the National Flute Association, and has received numerous grants and honors, including from New Music USA and The Fromm Foundation. EQ continues to curate a catalog of new works that fully exploit the dynamic expressive capabilities of four flutes together. title: Music from the Dark Side
description: $15 admission / 7:30 doors / standing / all ages Three music projects explore moody aspects of folk, darkwave and ritual, shamanic sounds and vocals. Featuring Winds of Alluria, Shadowmerge, and Ajda the Turkish Queen. WINDS OF ALLURIA Enchanting female vocals from Eurasian Shaman Khaluna Kam. Together with Totem Faehy's incredible throat singing and natural connection to animism, he brings an element sound balance. Heavy ritual ancestral sounds, authentic shamanic vocals, throat and overtone singing, and kulning. Their unique vocal abilities create a memorable journey of sound rooted in ancient traditions of ritual and lore. https://windsofalluria.bandcamp.com/ SHADOWMERGE Shadowmerge is the latest project from veteran Boston guitarist Doug Vargas and singer/poet Marlene Tholl. This ambient darkwave collaboration explores the evolution of ethereal alternative rock, poetry, and song — a moody mix of Vargas' atmospheric guitar and Tholl's haunting vocals and emotionally charged spoken word. This Lilypad performance marks the release of their new EP, E-Life, which grapples with the complex challenges of modern life through haunting soundscapes and post-rock textures. Following their previous release, Weight of Forever, E-Life marks a shift toward a more driving, ethereal sound. https://shadowmerge.bandcamp.com/ AJDA THE TURKISH QUEEN Ajda the Turkish Queen is a singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who typically performs on guitar and mandolin. Currently focused on solo endeavors including her forthcoming second solo album “Only Child", she will perform some of those very autumnal tunes at this show. She is founder of bands such as Black Fortress of Opium and the Ronnie James Dio tribute AjDIO. Influences include artists like Little Jimmy Scott, Nick Cave, PJ Harvey, Nico, Ute Lemper, Siouxsie Sioux, Ella Fitzgerald, and more, as well as the lonesome voices of Turkish muezzins. https://ajdatheturkishqueen.bandcamp.com/

The panel features Professor Mimi Ito, Director of the Connected Learning Lab, Professor Sherry Turkle, founding director of the MIT Initiative on Technology and Self, and Mike Rizkalla, CEO & Founder of Snorble, a visionary leader in AI, consumer robotics, humanoid robotics, and children's technology. 2027 Arthur Miller Lecture on Science and Ethics There are many views surrounding the advances in children's toys with artificial intelligence capabilities. From a sociological standpoint, some experts believe children should not be the consumers of relational AI, programs that pretend to have a self, capable of humanlike connection. Chatbots draw us into a game of pretend — and for some, pretend empathy becomes empathy enough. While the seductions of pretend empathy are dangerous for all of us, children have no defense; they are first-time learners. Others in the field view the advent of these new computers, or robots and physical AI, as a chance to change the outcomes we build for ourselves and to realign incentives. Joy, laughter, and love can be something different to everyone. To a child, it is having someone to play with. To a parent, it is five minutes where nothing is going wrong. To a grandparent, it is seeing their family happy. Embodied AI is a blank canvas. A new mix of cameras, sensors, voice, character, and context gives us a whole new toolkit to do good things, to help people in ways that were never available before. We need to stop running in the other direction and embrace the tech before it becomes weaponized. title: Cities of Islamic Art: From Historical Visual Systems to the Formation of Contemporary Islamic Art in North America
description: Featuring artist Laurelie Rae. This lecture uses Cities of Islamic Art, Vol. 2 as both an object and a methodology to examine Islamic art as a mobile system of visual knowledge rather than a fixed historical style. Beginning with historical surfaces from Isfahan, Istanbul, Damascus, Cairo, and Granada, the talk traces how motifs migrate across ceramics, tiles, manuscripts, and architecture to form the fabric of visual culture and heritage known as “Islamic Art.” The lecture then shifts to the speaker’s doctoral research, examining how these visual systems are reframed and redefined by visual and sonic artists within the North American diaspora context. The artist’s book functions here as a curatorial and analytical device—a way of reorganizing visual knowledge outside conventional art historical and museological categories. No registration required.

title: Spookey Ruben
description: Spookey Ruben Spookey Ruben @spookeyruben Alice Cohen @alicedesoda Monkey @meammonkey The Freakshadows @hanfreitasmusic + DJ mXe @basicbitch42069 ARTIST BIOS: Spookey Ruben is undoubtedly a household name in the Canadian indie scene, an artist who has stayed unmistakably authentic across three decades. Emerging in the mid-1990s, he has built a body of work defined by playful eccentricity and an intuitive grasp of pop that never sacrifices curiosity in favor of convention. Spookey’s music is a sophisticated combination of childlike wonder, formal experimentation, and melodic discipline, aging into something closer to prophecy than nostalgia. Born Alan Deil in Ottawa, Spookey spent much of his childhood moving through Europe, where his father worked as an engineer for the European Space Agency. A restless adolescence in Germany and the Netherlands gave way to thrash metal, long hair, and the nickname “Spooky”, later stylized as the instantly recognizable “Spookey.” Settling in Washington, D.C. in his high school years, Spookey formed the band Transilience , whose 1990 release Mouthful of Buildings became a cornerstone of avant-garde thrash jazz. He then moved to Toronto at nineteen to study film at York University. There, he drifted back toward music, accumulating ideas on a home four-track that would become the foundation of Spookey Ruben. Those bedroom recordings became Modes of Transportation Vol. 1 , a debut that immediately set him apart from his contemporaries. Crowned “Pet Sounds of the 90s”, the album catapulted him into critical acclaim through its densely imagined world: fairy-tale introductions, yodeling vocals, lullabies that drifted into darkness, and collage-like sound design sitting comfortably alongside impeccably crafted pop hooks. Drawing from the elasticity and moods of 1980s British new wave while filtering those influences through his distinctly personal lens, Spookey established a musical language that felt both referential and entirely his own.

title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood . title: Physical Math Seminar
description: Speaker: Olivia Pomerenk (Brown University) Title: Flocking and floating: collective behavior in fluid systems Abstract: Collective behavior emerges across biological scales, from the self-assembly of particles and cells to the coordinated motion of insects, fish, and birds. This talk explores mathematical approaches to two examples of collective behavior in fluid environments: passive particles interacting through a deformable interface at the capillary scale, and active agents interacting through wakes at the inertial scale. In the first half, we develop a generalized boundary-element framework for capillary interactions among arbitrary three-dimensional particle assemblies at a fluid interface. An iterative approach identifies equilibrium configurations while allowing for particle tilting and nontrivial contact-line geometry. This provides a general framework for characterizing how particle geometry and assembly configurations produce attraction, repulsion, and collective organization, with applications ranging from cellular and sub-cellular self-assembly to insects at the air-water interface. In the second half, we shift from passive particles to active agents, and from the capillary to the inertial scale. We develop a reduced-order model of the wake-vortex interactions between two flapping birds flying in tandem. The model retains essential unsteady flapping dynamics while remaining computationally tractable, enabling optimization over a six-dimensional state space comprising the follower's three-dimensional relative position and three independent flapping parameters. Applying the model to northern bald ibises, we identify an optimal configuration that minimizes the follower bird's aerodynamic power expenditure, and use these results to investigate the aerodynamic mechanisms underlying V-formations. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? His teaching draws upon his experience in the classroom, rehearsal room, and on the Broadway stage to help dancers integrate technique, musicality, character, and storytelling. description: $15 / $10 students / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated Bruce Gertz Quintet Jeff Stout, trumpet Rick DiMuzio, tenor Russell Hoffmann, piano Bruce Gertz, bass Gary Fieldman, drums Bruce's new solo recordings are like meditations that vibrate in the solar plexus and resonate through your being. His command of the instrument and imagination are an elixir for being transported to the pure music channel. Bravo Bruce - Jerry Bergonzi Every morning, world-renowned jazz bassist, composer, and educator, Bruce Gertz, makes himself a cup of coffee and sits at the baby grand piano of his Melrose, MA living room. Surrounded by quirky plants, records of his esteemed inspirations, and albums of his own, Gertz composes something every day, regardless of the day’s events ahead. He says, "Sometimes I only get a short idea but that can be the seed of a beautiful composition." His counterparts applaud him for his restless commitment to self-improvement. Gertz is known for his superb mastery of the upright bass and was named “Outstanding Bassist” by Boston Music Awards. What some fans don’t know is that he grew up playing electric bass from the age of 14 and still plays (and teaches) the electric quite often. His extraordinary contribution to music education has earned him multiple recognition awards from The International Association of Jazz Educators and the Jazz Education Network. He has been serving as a Professor of Bass at Berklee College of Music since 1976. Additional educator credits include serving on the advisory board of the International Society of Bassists and as an adjudicator at the Clark Terry UNH Jazzer's Festival. Gertz has performed and recorded with such artists as Gary Burton, Jerry Bergonzi, John Abercrombie, Joey Calderazzo, Kenny Werner, Mick Goodrick, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Billy Hart, Bill Frisell, Bob Berg, George Cables, Gil Evans, Tom Harrell, Jon Hendricks, Diane Schuur, Dave Brubeck, George Garzone, Mike Stern, Larry Coryell, Joe Lovano, Cab Calloway, Maynard Fer

Class is taught ELEF (Everybody Leads Everybody Follows), which helps you better understand how both roles work and feel, so that beyond this series, you can choose the one that suits you, or choose to keep dancing in both! Balboa is a vernacular swing dance from Southern California in the 1920s and 30s, and is indebted to the African-American roots and culture of Swing Jazz and Swing dancing. We encourage everyone to explore the history of this dance, the dancers that created it in Southern California, and the music and musicians that made it possible. Balboa today is an improvisational, joyful partner dance with a vibrant worldwide community, evolving into the present while honoring its origins. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? July and Stan have danced Balboa since the early 2000s, learning from original SoCal dancers and the second-generation teachers who came after them. We both deeply love social partner-dancing, and we teach so that more people can participate in this joyful community of movement and connection. Pandit Das was the pioneer of kathak dance bringing his rich training and upbringing in Kolkata, India to the US in 1971. I began my studies informally in 1997 while at Tufts University with Gretchenji and was hooked. From 2003 to 2011 I trained, taught, and toured as a member of the Chitresh Das Dance Company (CDDC) all across the US and India, holding lead roles such as Sita in Sita Haran. I have been steeped in this incredibly rich tradition of kathak, with it’s elements of dance, music, history, philosophy, math, and so much more and am thrilled to share with students and audiences widely in a manner that highlights how universal and accessible and FUN it really is! description: No dance experience is needed to join this class! Latina Tribe is a dance fitness method primarily influenced by reggaeton and contemporary Latin music, while also incorporating elements of hip-hop, pop, and other dance styles. Reggaeton developed through a blend of Caribbean and Latin American influences, with roots in Panama and Puerto Rico and strong connections to reggae en español, dancehall, and hip-hop. Today, the genre has grown into a global cultural movement while remaining deeply connected to the Latin and Caribbean communities that shaped it. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I am a certified Senior Instructor with Latina Tribe, a dance fitness method focused on creating empowering spaces for women and members of the LGBTQ+ community. I began my journey with Latina Tribe as a student in 2021 and, after years of practicing the method, became a certified instructor and began teaching in 2024. Since then, I have continued my training and recently earned the Senior Instructor designation, which allows me to teach across all levels of the method. My main goal is to connect with every person that steps in my classes, creating a space where movement, fitness, community, and self-expression come together. description: Postpartum Movement is a welcoming, supportive space to move, reconnect, and care for yourself during the postpartum journey. Cost: $0 – $22 Sliding Scale REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Majestic Healing Pathways™ is the foundational care model that guides all of Majestic Community Wellness’s programs. It reflects our belief that healing is a right — not a privilege — and that healing happens most sustainably when care is consistent, culturally grounded, and rooted in community. Developed in response to gaps in traditional health and wellness systems, Majestic Healing Pathways™ centers the lived experiences of Black and Brown communities who face disproportionate stress, trauma, and barriers to care. The model honors the reality that healing is not a single intervention, but a pathway built over time through breath, movement, rest, relationship, and choice. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? For more than 20 years, Nora has been teaching yoga and dance to students of all ages. She completed her 200-hour teacher training at Atmananda Yoga, and her teaching continues to be informed by years of study in Pilates, Feldenkrais, Hot Yoga, and Katonah Yoga. The births of her two children inspired her to deepen her studies in prenatal and postnatal yoga. She focused much of her teaching on supporting families and children through the various stages of development. During this time, she earned her Prenatal Yoga Certification through OM Yoga
